neuroai.name: Intention & Action
neuroai.summary: The shared DCC/DCCN programme studies integration of rules, percepts and concepts into instrumental and communicative actions, including predictive action mechanisms, shared conceptual frames and control of emotional actions. These are explicit sensorimotor-control and representation mechanisms with a credible computational bridge; the page does not claim an AI prototype.
neuroai.activity: The canonical DCCN page names Ivan Toni as PI, lists current guest scientist, postdocs and PhD candidates, and records ERC and NWO-STW programmes running through 2027. The live DCC page and current Donders Theme 2 directory identify the same named group and Ivan Toni, so this is one programme rather than two units.

neuroai.name: Inter-Individual Brain Dynamics Collaboration Unit
neuroai.institution: RIKEN CBS–TOYOTA Collaboration Center, RIKEN Center for Brain Science
neuroai.summary: This separately named current RIKEN/Toyota collaboration unit studies neural bases of social communication and well-being using hyperscanning fMRI, psychological experiments and mathematical models. A 2024 official award identifies its unit leader and a recent perceptual-decision study. The specific social-brain mechanism is central cognition with an explicit computational bridge, while it does not claim a general artificial-intelligence programme.
neuroai.activity: Official Dec 2024 award record names Koike as unit leader and reports the JCSS 2024 presentation award for research on psychological pressure and perceptual decision-making; current unit page lists active lab members and its methods.

neuroai.name: Interactive Robot Learning Laboratory

neuroai.name: International Centre for Neuromorphic Systems

neuroai.name: International Research Center for Neurointelligence (WPI-IRCN)

bio-inspired.summary: Studies active regulation of plasma-membrane and actomyosin-cortex organization, mechanical heterogeneity, mechanosensing and endocytic trafficking. The cell-scale organization is explicit; its relation to Bio-inspired information processing is inferred.
bio-inspired.activity: Current lab and research pages list current 2024–2026 research on cell volume regulation, cortex mechanics and membrane signaling; the 2026 symposium talk details actomyosin/endocytic regulation of membrane heterogeneity.

bio-inspired.name: Cellular Computations and Learning Group
bio-inspired.institution: Max Planck Institute for Neurobiology of Behavior — caesar
bio-inspired.summary: The group explicitly develops theories and experiments for information processing and learning in single cells, including biochemical signal integration, memory, and response generalization. This directly matches the cellular/molecular computation and basal cognition themes.
bio-inspired.activity: The 2026 KITP programme lists Koseska speaking on biological computations and learning without attractors; a 2024 peer-reviewed article is affiliated with the current lab and studies biological computation in signaling networks.

bio-inspired.name: Cellular Learning, Adaptation & Control Group
bio-inspired.institution: Technion — Israel Institute of Technology, Department of Chemical Engineering and Network Biology Research Laboratories
bio-inspired.summary: The group explicitly studies learning, adaptation and control in brainless biological systems such as cells and cell populations, including exploratory dynamics in biological networks.
bio-inspired.activity: First-party publications include “Identifying dynamic regulation with machine learning using adversarial surrogates” (2025), 2024 work on bacterial growth-rate/phenotypic distributions, and 2026 current outputs; the institutional page lists Brenner as professor and group head.

bio-inspired.name: Centre of Excellence on Biologically Inspired Robots and Drones (CoE-BIRD)
bio-inspired.institution: Indian Institute of Technology Delhi
bio-inspired.summary: CoE-BIRD is a formally recognized interdisciplinary centre on biologically inspired robots and drones. Its current soft/compliant robotics theme explicitly develops bio-inspired morphologies and mechanisms, including morphological computation, matching the published Bio-inspired themes. This centre-level programme is distinct from its separately identified child lab.
bio-inspired.activity: A current 2026 CoE-BIRD project is supervised by Bhasin and Roy and is hosted in JATC Soft Robotics Lab; the official April 2026 IIT Delhi newsletter names Bhasin as current CoE-BIRD coordinator. The centre itself is formally recognized and its live theme page lists its current research direction.

bio-inspired.name: Chair of Physics of Synthetic Biological Systems (Simmel Lab)
bio-inspired.institution: Technical University of Munich, School of Natural Sciences, Department of Bioscience
bio-inspired.summary: Current work explicitly aims to build self-organizing molecular/cellular systems that sense, compute, move and act; research includes DNA/RNA computing, cell-free synthetic cells, synthetic gene circuits, intercellular communication and programmed pattern formation. This is a direct molecular/cellular computation unit.
bio-inspired.activity: The official members page lists Simmel as group leader and Bienau as a current PhD student; the publication page lists 2026 DNA molecular robotics and 2025–26 synthetic biology outputs.

bio-inspired.name: Chair of Statistical Field Theory (CSFT), EPFL
bio-inspired.institution: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)
bio-inspired.summary: EPFL CSFT explicitly identifies artificial life, especially discrete and continuous cellular automata, as a key project area. Current postdoc Barbora Hudcová studies complex systems as ALife models, formal cellular-automata dynamics, self-replication and computational capacity; the group organized a 2026 ALIFE complexity workshop on cellular automata and emergent patterns. This is an explicit current artificial-life programme within a broader statistical field theory chair.
bio-inspired.activity: Current CSFT page lists artificial life/cellular automata among key projects and a May 2026 workshop; the current roster lists Hudcová as postdoc. Her current research page and 2026 EPFL event details provide recent substantive activity.

bio-inspired.name: Chao Zhong Laboratory — Materials Synthetic Biology
bio-inspired.institution: Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Institute of Synthetic Biology / Materials Synthetic Biology Center
bio-inspired.summary: The group builds programmable recombinase circuits that cause a founder cell to generate descendant populations at predicted, tunable ratios and with distinct functions. The current work explicitly frames cellular differentiation as computation and connects controlled lineage branching to multicellular organization and morphogenesis.
bio-inspired.activity: Official March 2026 SIAT report and lab publication list document the jointly led Nature study: recombinase switches program cell fate branches and descendant ratios; a mathematical model predicts outcomes; engineered populations divide functional tasks. Current lab roster lists active PI, faculty and trainees.

bio-inspired.name: Chemical Origins of Life Laboratory (COoL) — Sudha Rajamani
bio-inspired.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Pune
bio-inspired.summary: The COoL lab studies how chemistry transitioned to biology through prebiotic polymers, self-assembly, replication and membranes that formed early cellular life. Current institutional page identifies Rajamani as professor and provides a substantive, mechanism-focused group programme.
bio-inspired.activity: The institutional profile was updated 17 June 2026, identifies her current professorship and current COoL lab projects on protocell emergence, prebiotic chemistry and early Earth analogue sites.

bio-inspired.name: Chemical Origins of Molecular Biology Group — John Sutherland
bio-inspired.institution: MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology
bio-inspired.summary: Sutherland’s current group page explicitly targets chemical origins of molecular biology through prebiotically plausible synthesis of information-bearing, catalytic and compartment-forming molecules, including RNA, translation, and lipids. Current group identity and 2025 activity are independently confirmed by MRC LMB.
bio-inspired.activity: MRC LMB’s 2025 report identifies Sutherland as an active Group Leader and describes the continuing group’s work on prebiotic pathways and the chemical origins of cellular format, central dogma, and genetic code.

bio-inspired.name: Cheng Zhang Group — DNA Molecular Circuits and Computing
bio-inspired.institution: Peking University, School of Computer Science
bio-inspired.summary: First-party lab scope explicitly includes complex DNA molecular circuit/computing; PKU profile documents 2026 peer-reviewed work.
bio-inspired.activity: Official PKU page lists 2026 Conformation-programmed DNA computing publication and identifies Zhang’s current faculty lab.

bio-inspired.name: Christopher Aaron O’Hara — Computational Disclosure / Autopoiesis Programme
bio-inspired.institution: Independent researcher; Crossref paper affiliation: Global Center for Advanced Studies (GCAS)
bio-inspired.city: Dublin (paper affiliation only; current location not established)
bio-inspired.summary: This current individual-led computational programme uses a self-modifying system to make organizational closure/autopoiesis assumptions explicit and testable. The ALIFE 2026 paper combines compositional graph reasoning for macro-action discovery with modal temporal logic verification and repeated-run stability analysis; a public code repository contains the executable model, DSL, metrics and validation helpers. The paper explicitly states this is not proof of life. It is therefore strongly related to grounded computational inquiry into living organization, not a claim of biological life, self-replication or experimentally validated autopoiesis.
bio-inspired.activity: The Aug 2026 ALIFE paper and companion code are the active project; current author README says he is extending second-order cybernetics/modal logic to emergence and autopoiesis.

bio-inspired.name: Chrystopher Nehaniv — artificial life and biological computation program
bio-inspired.institution: University of Waterloo
bio-inspired.summary: A current artificial-life and complex adaptive systems program includes automata, gene-regulatory networks, differentiated multicellularity, and cellular automata models of self-reproduction and evolution.
bio-inspired.activity: Current full professor; co-organized the 2025 Distributed Ciphers session, whose stated scope includes biological computation, self-replication, morphogenesis and gene regulation.

bio-inspired.name: Chunhai Fan Research Group — SJTU DNA Storage Research Center
bio-inspired.institution: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Zhangjiang Advanced Research Institute
bio-inspired.summary: The PI-led group has published molecular systems that implement general-purpose DNA computation and a DNA-framework state machine in living cells. The 2025 storage paper confirms current team activity, while the computational mechanisms identified are in 2023 work.
bio-inspired.activity: Jan 2025 official center release identifies the Fan-led team’s DNA information-storage research; the current profile retains DNA computation and lists the 2023 gate-array and living-cell state-machine papers.

bio-inspired.name: Claes Strannegård — ecosystem agent-modelling programme
bio-inspired.institution: University of Gothenburg, Department of Applied IT, division CLIC
bio-inspired.summary: An active PI-led computational ecosystem programme models plants, animals and abiotic environments. Its animal agents use homeostasis, learning and decision-making, with reinforcement learning or genetic algorithms to balance survival needs and reproduce predator-prey dynamics. The artificial-life/open-endedness fit is inferred from this mechanism evidence.
bio-inspired.activity: NAISS-funded project Ecosystems, PI Claes Strannegård, started 2026-09-25 and runs to 2027-10-01. The project description specifies ecosystem modelling with homeostatic agents using reinforcement learning or genetic algorithms.

bio-inspired.name: Cognitive Developmental Robotics Lab (Nagai Lab)
bio-inspired.institution: The University of Tokyo, IRCN
bio-inspired.summary: The lab uses computational and robotic methods to study cognitive development, including sensorimotor predictive learning and developmental mechanisms.
bio-inspired.activity: Official lab sources list current 2026 papers and presentations.

bio-inspired.name: Cognitive Neuroimaging Lab — Metabolic Connectivity Program
bio-inspired.institution: Monash University
bio-inspired.summary: The lab measures dynamic brain glucose metabolism and metabolic connectivity to understand cognition and aging; Jamadar coauthored the 2025 review on metabolic costs of cognition.
bio-inspired.activity: Official profile lists an active metabolic-connectivity research program and 2025 research outputs.

bio-inspired.name: Collective Cellular Dynamics Laboratory (Tamal Das)
bio-inspired.institution: Tata Institute of Fundamental Research Hyderabad
bio-inspired.summary: The lab studies collective epithelial dynamics and tissue morphogenesis. Current mechanochemical work treats organelles as integrators of geometry, tension and biochemical signaling that control cell fate and leader emergence during wound healing and collective migration.
bio-inspired.activity: The 2025 interview reports ongoing cell competition/morphogenesis work; the 2026 abstract for his current talk describes mechanochemical information processing and collective cell decisions; TIFR lists current research areas.

bio-inspired.name: Collective Dynamics research group, University of Bristol
bio-inspired.lead: Professor Jonathan Lawry; core team includes Chanelle Lee
bio-inspired.institution: University of Bristol
bio-inspired.summary: The current group studies system-level function emerging from interacting parts across biology, engineering and social science, with explicit modelling methods. Its current core members Chanelle Lee and Jonathan Lawry coauthored a 2026 Neural Cellular Automata method in which local learned updates produce emergent message passing and map completion. The paper gives a direct computational self-organisation/neural cellular automata connection, without claiming biological morphogenesis or life.
bio-inspired.activity: Current official group pages list the group and its methods; the people roster lists Lawry and Lee as core team. The 2026 paper code repository documents the exact NeuralCA model and multi-agent mapping experiments; current official Bristol pages list recent 2026 research activity by group members.

bio-inspired.name: Complex Adaptive System Laboratory (Takadama Lab)
bio-inspired.institution: The University of Tokyo, Graduate School of Information Science and Technology
bio-inspired.summary: Takadama's group explicitly derives open-ended learning and continuously growing AI from biological evolution and developmental processes, generating new tasks, morphologies, and strategies rather than only solving predefined problems.
bio-inspired.activity: Presentations at the Evolutionary Computation Symposium 2025 and a JSAI journal interview with Prof. Takadama; lab page copyright 2026.

bio-inspired.name: Complex Adaptive Systems and Computational Intelligence (CASCI) research group
bio-inspired.institution: Binghamton University, School of Systems Science and Industrial Engineering; Católica Biomedical Research Center collaboration
bio-inspired.summary: CASCI has an active, explicitly named research programme developing canalization and schema-redescription methods for automata networks used to model gene regulation and biochemical signalling. The group links network redundancy to cellular activity, causal control, dynamical modularity and collective computation in intracellular systems. This is a computational methods programme for cellular/molecular systems, rather than generic complex-systems research. The exact ALIFE 2026 paper title matches this current line, though publisher access prevented reading its full text in this pass.
bio-inspired.activity: CASCI page updated August 2026 shows current group roster, current PI role and current operations; Luis Rocha’s 2026 talks include a presentation on redundancy and modularity of biochemical regulation and network dynamics; CASCI page links active research and selected publications.

bio-inspired.name: Complex Quantum Systems
bio-inspired.institution: University of Maryland, Baltimore County
bio-inspired.summary: Studies computational resources in physical dynamics and the foundations of statistical mechanics. Natural computation is an explicit research theme.
bio-inspired.activity: Current CQS roster names Anza as PI and Hahn as PhD student. Anza organized Information Engines 2026 and presented geometric quantum dynamics. A January 2026 university report describes his Physics Co-Pilot programme.

bio-inspired.name: Complex Systems Lab (Ricard Solé)
bio-inspired.institution: Institute of Evolutionary Biology (IBE), Spanish National Research Council (CSIC) and Pompeu Fabra University (UPF); ICREA
bio-inspired.summary: The Complex Systems Lab studies evolutionary origins of complex systems through mathematical models and synthetic-biology experiments, including protocells, cognition, cellular circuits and artificial systems in silico. Ricard Solé coauthored Eco-Evo-Devox, a modular artificial-life platform that makes ecology, development and embodied neural evolution jointly manipulable. This direct current paper link supports an inferred bridge from the lab’s broader synthetic and artificial-systems programme to Bio-inspired developmental and neural-evolution research; it does not establish a separately named neural-evolution subunit.
bio-inspired.activity: Ricard Solé coauthored the 2025 ALIFE proceedings paper describing Eco-Evo-Devox, an artificial-life platform for ecological and developmental roots of neural evolution. The current IBE lab page names him PI and lists ongoing synthetic-ecosystem work, current lab members and 2026 publications; the lab remit explicitly includes artificial systems and cognition.

bio-inspired.name: Complexity and Astrobiology Group — Jacobo Aguirre
bio-inspired.institution: Centro de Astrobiología (CAB, CSIC-INTA), Molecular Evolution Department
bio-inspired.summary: This named research group applies mathematical and computational models, complexity theory and network science to the origin and early evolution of life, including whether diversity, inheritance and replication can emerge naturally from simple models.
bio-inspired.activity: The CAB 2024 annual report lists ongoing doctoral projects on modeling life’s origin as a complex emergent process and emergence of life from complexity theory; the current CAB profile confirms Aguirre’s CSIC Distinguished Researcher role and origin-of-life modelling remit. The linked external group page returned 404 in this check, so no current member roster is claimed.

bio-inspired.name: Computational Cell Biology (Mukund Thattai)
bio-inspired.institution: National Centre for Biological Sciences, TIFR
bio-inspired.summary: Uses quantitative models and cell biology to study how molecular interactions and vesicle traffic organize intracellular systems and regulate distributed biochemical activity; the cell is explicitly framed as a logical/computational machine.
bio-inspired.activity: Mukund Thattai authored a 2026 review on the evolution and operation of eukaryotic membrane traffic, alongside a current NCBS profile and research page.

bio-inspired.name: Computational Cell Fate
bio-inspired.institution: Radboud Institute for Molecular Life Sciences, Radboud University
bio-inspired.summary: The group models how individual cells process cell-cell and environmental signals, communicate across scales and make robust fate decisions, using mechanistic biophysics and single-cell data. This is a specific cellular information-processing bridge; its computational approach does not by itself define the relevance.
bio-inspired.activity: The first-party group page reports an August 2026 Cell Systems paper on heterogeneous cell-cell communication and September 2026 group hires; its current group roster and methods page corroborate ongoing programme.

bio-inspired.name: Computational Immunology Group (Radboud University / Radboudumc)
bio-inspired.institution: Radboud University, Institute for Computing and Information Sciences, and Radboud University Medical Center, Department of Medical BioSciences
bio-inspired.summary: The group explicitly studies how adaptive immune cells process information, learn and collaborate to make collective decisions. Current projects combine AI, biophysical simulations and immune-cell data to decode immune responses, and the Artificial Immunological Intelligence programme uses immune-system learning to inform both immunology and machine learning. This directly fits cellular/basal cognition and collective-cell intelligence; no broader ordinary immunology inference is needed.
bio-inspired.activity: Current official project pages include “AI and Simulations for Decoding the Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Immune Responses” (2023–2028) and “Artificial Immunological Intelligence” (2020–2026). The group’s publication list includes 2025 GECCO output and 2026 T-cell immunology and collective-behaviour papers; its current roster names Textor (Associate Professor) and Wortel (Assistant Professor).

bio-inspired.name: Computational Intelligence Group
bio-inspired.institution: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Department of Computer Science
bio-inspired.summary: The active group develops systems that self-organize, evolve, and learn, including evolutionary computing and robotics; the 2025 robot-fertility paper directly extends evolved robot populations.
bio-inspired.activity: Current group roster/vision and current 2025 GECCO output identify the active evolutionary-robotics program.

bio-inspired.name: Computational Magnetic Metamaterials (COMET)
bio-inspired.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering; cross-department Computer Science and Electronic Systems researchers
bio-inspired.summary: COMET investigates artificial life and unconventional computation in physical materials, especially artificial spin ice. Its current nanomagnetic work uses evolutionary algorithms to discover life-like patterns in a material substrate, including gliders and interacting “creatures,” and studies their computation and low-power computing potential. This directly fits the Bio-inspired in-materio/physical computation and artificial-life boundary without asserting biological motivation.
bio-inspired.activity: COMET’s current NTNU research-initiative page lists SPrINTER (2022–2028) and NTNU Enabling Technologies Nano (2023–2027); the 2026 peer-reviewed article reports emergent life-like creatures in artificial spin ice, evolutionary search and an experimental demonstration, with NTNU coauthors Penty, Jensen and Tufte. NTNU’s current 2026 conference page also lists their follow-on artificial-life-in-materio presentation.

bio-inspired.name: Computing, Intelligence, and Communications Lab (CCTL)
bio-inspired.institution: Chonnam National University
bio-inspired.summary: The lab’s funded research includes DNA computing systems and algorithms for large-scale artificial neural networks and DNA memory software/hardware, rather than DNA merely as a data label.
bio-inspired.activity: Current page reports a sole-PI 2025–2028 National Research Foundation of Korea DNA-computing award.

bio-inspired.name: Cortical Labs
bio-inspired.institution: Cortical Labs
bio-inspired.summary: The company’s official research page lists ongoing research on biological neural networks, closed-loop neural interfaces, learning performance and synthetic biological intelligence.
bio-inspired.activity: Official research page publishes a 2026 paper list and active platform research; corporate unit accepted as R&D organization.

bio-inspired.name: Creative Algorithms Lab
bio-inspired.institution: McMaster University, Department of Computing and Software
bio-inspired.summary: The current lab describes its programme as nature-inspired computing, investigates emergent memory and hierarchy in digital evolution for dynamic partially observable predictive control, and includes current evolutionary-robotics and neurobiologically inspired AI projects. The ALIFE paper on genetically evolved program teams and shared memory is part of this active line. The lab spans computing and art; relevance rests on its explicit active evolutionary and bio-inspired AI programme, not on generic artistic work.
bio-inspired.activity: Current lab page lists active lab membership and recent projects in bio-inspired AI, self-organization, evolutionary computation, and evolutionary robotics; its publications page lists 2025 ALIFE and 2026 GECCO/Evo* work in the same TPG/evolutionary-learning programme.

bio-inspired.name: Creative Machines Lab
bio-inspired.institution: Columbia University
bio-inspired.summary: The lab builds self-replicating, self-modeling, creative machines explicitly inspired by biology, with current 2024-2026 student projects including machine cognition and embodiment.
bio-inspired.activity: People page lists Adidev Jhunjhunwala (2026-) Machine Cognition and Embodiment, Eli Gross (2026-) Intuitive Scientific Discovery, Richard Milvenan (2024-) Edge Dynamical Modeling.

bio-inspired.name: Cristian Rojas — UNILA molecular biosensing and genetic-engineering research programme
bio-inspired.institution: Federal University for Latin American Integration (UNILA), Latin American Institute of Life and Nature Sciences
bio-inspired.summary: Current Rojas-supervised work includes a CRISPR-Cas12a dengue-detection system and DNA-aptamer detection projects, alongside his molecular/synthetic-biology research programme. The information-processing bridge is inferred from programmable molecular recognition and signal detection; the sources do not establish logic-gate computation or a general-purpose molecular computer.
bio-inspired.activity: UNILA’s 2025 official projects listing includes Rojas-supervised projects on DNA aptamers for detecting and neutralizing multidrug-resistant bacteria, recombinant-enzyme production and synthetic-biology methods. UNILA’s 2025 report records a supervised CRISPR-Cas12a dengue wastewater detection project; the 2025 UNILA graduate roster records the corresponding master’s defense. Current UNILA faculty records list Rojas in 2026 teaching and leadership.

bio-inspired.name: Crutchfield computational mechanics and information-engines programme
bio-inspired.institution: Complexity Sciences Center, University of California, Davis
bio-inspired.summary: Develops computational mechanics, learning dynamics, evolving cellular automata and physical information engines. Current momentum-computing work addresses energy, speed and fidelity constraints.
bio-inspired.activity: August 2026 programme records Crutchfield’s momentum-computing talk, including implementations and energy bounds. Current PI page identifies him as CSC director and Distinguished Professor.

bio-inspired.name: Cyber-physical Systems Group — Heiko Hamann
bio-inspired.institution: University of Konstanz, Department of Computer and Information Science
bio-inspired.summary: Current group work includes evolutionary robotics, swarm robotics, bio-hybrid systems and robot-plant systems. This maps directly to evolutionary robotics and body–brain co-design.
bio-inspired.activity: Personal research page last updated 2026-10-12 and lists 2026 evolutionary multi-robot publications; official group page lists active 2025/26 courses and research.

bio-inspired.name: Daniel Hexner — trainable materials and physical learning research programme
bio-inspired.institution: Technion – Israel Institute of Technology, Faculty of Mechanical Engineering
bio-inspired.summary: A PI-led physical-learning programme trains disordered matter to learn desired mechanical responses; its current first-party description explicitly relates learning, adaptability and memory to biology and shows an allostery-inspired response. This maps to the exact Bio physical-learning theme while the evidence does not establish measured energy savings or thermodynamic optimality.
bio-inspired.activity: Technion CRIS records publications in 2024, 2025 and 2026, including Mechanical regularization (2024), Designing precise dynamical steady states in disordered networks (2025), and Equilibrium Propagation for Dissipative Dynamics (2026). The current programme page describes ongoing research in trainable materials and open positions.

bio-inspired.name: Dasaradhi Palakodeti Lab — Model Systems to Study Regeneration
bio-inspired.institution: Institute for Stem Cell Science and Regenerative Medicine (inStem)
bio-inspired.summary: The lab investigates post-transcriptional regulatory networks, cell-state transitions and cell-fate decisions in planarian regeneration and embryonic-stem-cell differentiation. The planarian regeneration mechanism is directly in scope; a computation bridge is inferred and not asserted as an explicit AI programme.
bio-inspired.activity: Current faculty profile states ongoing work in regeneration and cell-state transitions; inStem recorded 2025–2026 research-lab hiring for Prof. Palakodeti’s lab.

bio-inspired.summary: Lab quantifies energy budgets for synapses and brain tissue and studies how brain energy supply constrains information-processing capacity and speed.
bio-inspired.activity: Official lab news lists a 2024 proof-of-principle study and 2026 centre/lab activity.

bio-inspired.summary: Current program develops foundations for thermodynamics of computation; recent work formalizes how to identify computations in natural dynamical systems.

bio-inspired.name: David Labonte animal biomechanics research programme
bio-inspired.institution: Imperial College London, Department of Bioengineering
bio-inspired.summary: Labonte's active programme studies the mechanical constraints that shape biological systems and evolutionary processes. His coauthored 2025 ALIFE work translates biological growth and age-related changes in animal power into a robotic locomotion curriculum. The link from this animal-mechanics programme to engineered systems is supported by that collaboration and is an inferred bridge; the programme itself is not classified as an evolutionary-robotics lab.

Labonte's current Imperial profile confirms his programme in animal biomechanics and evolutionary process mechanics.

bio-inspired.name: David Zamorano Sánchez laboratory — bacterial decision mechanisms
bio-inspired.institution: Centro de Ciencias Genómicas, Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México (UNAM)
bio-inspired.summary: The lab explicitly studies the molecular mechanisms governing bacterial decision-making and how two-component systems, alternative sigma factors and second messengers control social behavior and stress responses in Vibrio. A current mechanism example examines dynamic c-di-GMP regulation by OpaR/phosphodiesterases and resulting biofilm-matrix expression. This is direct research on cellular signal integration, state choice and collective microbial behavior within the basal-cognition/collective-cell-intelligence and cellular/molecular-processing themes. It is not a claim of sentience or engineered AI.
bio-inspired.activity: The CCG profile lists 2025 peer-reviewed activity on CRISPR/Cas transposition-system regulation in native V. parahaemolyticus. The 2023 OpaR paper is a specific mechanism/activity item showing dynamic c-di-GMP homeostasis and downstream biofilm gene regulation; CCG currently describes decision-making/signal-processing as the lab remit.

bio-inspired.name: Deans Lab
bio-inspired.institution: Georgia Institute of Technology
bio-inspired.summary: The group engineers genetic circuits to impose temporal and logical control over stem-cell differentiation and to create cells that sense and respond to disease; its stated work uses ML to identify cell-fate decision points.
bio-inspired.activity: Current lab roster lists active students and ongoing research; 2025 lab publications in cell engineering and circuit design are listed in current team material.

bio-inspired.institution: National Centre for Biological Sciences, TIFR
bio-inspired.summary: Models computation, feedback and decision-making in active cellular processes, chemical reaction networks and cooperative cell populations.
bio-inspired.activity: The 2024 study by Sandeep Krishna and collaborators analyzes relaxation dynamics in chemical reaction networks and relates reaction-network topology to cellular network behavior; official NCBS profile lists ongoing computation using active cellular processes.

bio-inspired.name: Developmental Epigenetics
bio-inspired.institution: Radboud Institute for Molecular Life Sciences, Radboud University
bio-inspired.summary: The group investigates cellular patterning, symmetry breaking, embryo development and cell-fate decisions using gastruloids, blastoids and stem-cell models. These are direct morphogenesis and developmental mechanisms.
bio-inspired.activity: The institutional group page lists active grants through 2028/29, 2025 publications and a current multi-person team; its research lines explicitly include patterning, symmetry breaking and cellular interactions.

bio-inspired.activity: Current lab roster lists D’Ambrosia as a graduate student; his August 2026 talk studies finite-precision computation and thermodynamic cost. The lab’s current site states active research across stat mech, learning and neuroscience.

bio-inspired.activity: The current group site names a 2025–2031 ERC Synergy award with Hannes Mutschler and lists multiple 2024–25 papers on protocell formation, RNA replication, prebiotic polymerization and chemical evolution.

bio-inspired.summary: The lab’s 2026 QD/Hebbian paper evolves diverse policies with local neuron-centric plasticity on RL tasks; its 2025 work applies QD to co-design soft-robot morphology and control. The underlying program is evolutionary and biologically inspired computation rather than biology-only data science.
bio-inspired.activity: 2026 University of Trento conference/proceedings activity and current self-reported Associate Professor role; repository lists two 2026 evo-computation papers.

bio-inspired.name: Diya Binoy Joseph Lab — Programming and Patterning of Epithelial Barriers
bio-inspired.institution: Institute for Stem Cell Science and Regenerative Medicine (inStem)
bio-inspired.summary: The lab studies how developmental cues pattern regionally specialized epithelial identity and organize immune-cell niches along tissue axes, using organotypic systems, spatial/single-cell methods and organoids. The exact biological patterning mechanism is explicit; its relevance to engineered or computational systems is inferred.
bio-inspired.activity: Her inStem PI page reports corresponding-author papers in Developmental Biology (April 2025) and Mucosal Immunology (September 2025), a 2026 urethral-organoid methods publication, and an independent laboratory active since 2022.

bio-inspired.name: DNA and Natural Algorithms Group (Caltech)
bio-inspired.institution: California Institute of Technology
bio-inspired.summary: Group studies biomolecular computation, DNA circuits, molecular programming, self-assembly and molecular robots.
bio-inspired.activity: DNA32 2026 volume includes a Winfree coauthored paper; official proceedings author affiliation and group page support current unit attribution.

researchPlans.title: DNA Group Research Agenda

bio-inspired.name: Dobata Lab
bio-inspired.institution: The University of Tokyo, Graduate School of Arts and Sciences
bio-inspired.summary: The current lab studies insect social and collective systems through empirical work, mathematical/computational analysis and simulation. Its current PI explicitly collaborates with engineers on ant-inspired swarm systems and uses robots as synthetic models to study how collective behavior emerges. This provides a direct biological-mechanism to engineered-swarm bridge that fits the Bio-inspired scope. The water-beetle paper is a concrete current collective-autonomy study; the fit does not depend on claiming that beetles are cells or on generalizing all ecology into AI.
bio-inspired.activity: Official publications page updated 2026-09-21 lists current 2026 insect collective papers and the 2025 ALIFE water-beetle study. The lab’s current 2025 reports include ongoing behavior tracking and collective-behavior work; official faculty page confirms PI role and active swarm-robotics collaboration.

bio-inspired.name: Donald H. Burke-Agüero Lab — RNA catalysis and origins of life
bio-inspired.institution: University of Missouri, Bond Life Sciences Center
bio-inspired.summary: The lab studies relationships among RNA sequence, function, selection, design, and evolution, including catalytic mechanisms relevant to early life.
bio-inspired.activity: The current ©2026 Bond LSC page identifies Burke-Agüero as PI and describes active lab themes; it explicitly states development of robust multiple-turnover ribozyme catalysts for engineered metabolism, synthetic biology, and origins-of-life applications.

bio-inspired.name: Dongrui Liu — Trustworthy AI / agent-evolution programme
bio-inspired.institution: Shanghai AI Laboratory
bio-inspired.summary: Current research-scientist programme leads and corresponds on named harness-policy co-evolution and self-evolving LLM-agent work.
bio-inspired.activity: Current Shanghai AI Lab Research Scientist page recruits researchers and lists 2026 outputs and SafeEvolve/SHE projects.

bio-inspired.name: Doron Lancet Lab — Systems Biology and Protobiology
bio-inspired.institution: Weizmann Institute of Science, Department of Molecular Genetics
bio-inspired.summary: The lab models early living organization as self-reproducing catalytic lipid assemblies. Its GARD work examines growth and fission, compositional inheritance, self-reproduction, selection and the transition from chemical to biological evolution.
bio-inspired.activity: The first-party publication list includes 2024 work on GARD prebiotic reproduction and order/complexity and 2026 work integrating composome and RNA-replicase origin models; the current lab page was updated in July 2026 and its group-members page in September 2026.

bio-inspired.name: Droplet Laboratory — Jitka Čejková group
bio-inspired.institution: Department of Chemical Engineering, University of Chemistry and Technology Prague (UCT Prague)
bio-inspired.summary: A current wet artificial-life group studies droplets as liquid robots and self-organizing chemical systems, including chemotactic and collective droplet behavior, life-like shape change, and cell encapsulation for microbial communication. This directly supports chemical/artificial-life and self-organizing biological-mechanism coverage.
bio-inspired.activity: The lab homepage lists 2026 events and research activity, identifies Čejková as lab lead, describes the group as a wet artificial-life lab, and reports that it accepts students. Its research page describes current study of droplet chemotaxis/collective behavior, chemical gardens and cell encapsulation for microbial communication.

bio-inspired.name: Duke DNA and Molecular Computing Program
bio-inspired.institution: Duke University
bio-inspired.summary: Duke’s official program describes DNA/RNA molecular-scale computation. The current Reif lab record lists active molecular-scale AI work and recent DNA-circuit papers; Nagipogu, a coauthor of the 2023 review, is listed as a current student.
bio-inspired.activity: The 2026-updated lab page lists current Molecular Assembly and Computation teaching and a current molecular-scale-AI graduate project; Duke ECE lists 2025 neural chemical-reaction-network learning and 2024 DNA computation papers.

bio-inspired.name: Dynamic Protocellular Systems — Dora Tang Lab
bio-inspired.institution: Saarland University
bio-inspired.summary: Tang’s current Saarland programme builds synthetic-cell and protocellular systems from molecular compartments and reactions. Its 2026 study of self-organizing artificial droplets that protect genetic material and regulate biochemical reactions directly investigates mechanisms of living-like organization and is relevant to the origins of cellular life.
bio-inspired.activity: Saarland University’s 2026 news report documents Tang-led work on artificial molecular droplets that self-organize, protect genetic material, and regulate biochemical reactions.

bio-inspired.name: Dynamical Systems Biology Lab — Jordi Garcia-Ojalvo
bio-inspired.institution: Universitat Pompeu Fabra, Department of Medicine and Life Sciences (MELIS)
bio-inspired.summary: The current lab explicitly links dynamical living systems to natural computation, information processing and learning. Its single-cell learning programme and CeLEARN work provide a direct mechanism-level fit to cellular/molecular computation and basal biological learning.
bio-inspired.activity: The UPF lab publications page lists 2024 papers on biological computation through recurrence and single-cell habituation and a 2025 paper on soft memory in recurrent biological networks. UPF’s 28 May 2026 report confirms Garcia-Ojalvo leads the lab and that it participates in CeLEARN, an ERC Synergy project on learning in single cells.

bio-inspired.name: Earth-Life Science Institute (ELSI)
bio-inspired.institution: Institute of Science Tokyo
bio-inspired.summary: Center-level identity is supported by its official establishment/mission page, its scope page, and multiple dated 2026 research outputs; separate PI-led children are retained only where their own identity/programme is independently evidenced.
bio-inspired.activity: Official homepage lists dated 2026 outputs including cellular thermodynamics, enzyme evolution, protocell-related chemistry and current institute activity.

bio-inspired.name: ECSO Lab — evolutionary cell physiology and origins of cellular complexity
bio-inspired.institution: Purdue University
bio-inspired.summary: The lab studies origins of eukaryotes and mitochondria, symbioses, and physiological/energetic constraints on cell evolution using large-scale phylogenetics, comparative genomics, bioinformatics, metagenomics, cultivation, and mathematical modeling.
bio-inspired.activity: Purdue’s current faculty page lists the assistant professor and 2024 work on energetic costs of cellular complexity; it describes an active research program on origins of major cell innovations and transitions.

bio-inspired.name: Eidosoma — Living Intelligence Research Lab
bio-inspired.institution: Eidosoma
bio-inspired.summary: Eidosoma is an explicitly identified current research lab directed by founder Robert Bjarnason. Its 2026 computational programme investigates how compositional inheritance can break, renew and be actively maintained in an origin-of-life GARD model, then tests related inheritance dynamics in cellular automata and gene-regulatory networks. Its current announced programme also addresses protocells, artificial life and distributed cell cognition. This is grounded life-organization and computational research; simulations are not evidence that autonomous life or a universal origin mechanism has been produced.
bio-inspired.activity: Founder-authored preprint/blog dated 2026-09-12 reports computational experiments using GARD, cellular automata and Wagner gene-regulatory networks to test inheritance break/renewal and interventions; public research record details reconstructions and limits. The official team page says Eidosoma was established in 2026 and names Bjarnason as founder.

bio-inspired.name: Eiko Matsuda — Human Harmony Design Science and Engineering programme
bio-inspired.institution: Keio University, Faculty of Science and Technology, Department of System Design Engineering
bio-inspired.summary: The current Keio researcher programme explicitly lists artificial life and embodied cognitive science and studies pre-representational sense-making, learning and human cognition, with findings embodied in AI, robots, VR and games. Recent ALIFE and 2025–2026 work make this an evidenced artificial-life/cognition programme; its connection to open-endedness is an inferred mechanism bridge.
bio-inspired.activity: Keio researcher page, updated 2026-08-07, lists current programme and 2025/2026 papers on pre-representational dynamic sense-making and embodied cognition; official faculty page confirms current assistant-professor appointment.

bio-inspired.name: Elias Barriga Group
bio-inspired.institution: TU Dresden, Cluster of Excellence Physics of Life
bio-inspired.summary: Studies the biophysical mechanisms by which endogenous electric and mechanical signals coordinate collective cell migration/differentiation, tissue morphogenesis, embryogenesis and regeneration. The computational relevance is an explicit inferred bridge from multi-cellular coordination and control, not a claim that the group builds AI.
bio-inspired.activity: The group roster identifies Barriga as current group leader and lists active trainees/postdocs; the 2026 HFSP award funds electrochemical actuation of tissue morphogenesis. The team includes Nunes, who is therefore covered here.

bio-inspired.name: Elisa Biondi PI programme at FfAME
bio-inspired.institution: Foundation for Applied Molecular Evolution, with joint appointment at Firebird Biomolecular Sciences
bio-inspired.summary: Biondi’s current PI programme studies prebiotic formation and evolution of informational molecules, RNA formation on mineral/geological surfaces and the evolutionary capacity of expanded genetic alphabets.
bio-inspired.activity: The current first-party PI profile says Biondi is PI/Fellow (2012–present), lists active projects on prebiotic informational molecules, and lists 2025 AEGIS replication and PNAS prebiotic RNA synthesis work. Current team directory labels her Principal Investigator & Fellow.

bio-inspired.name: Elisha Moses Lab — Physics of Biological Computation
bio-inspired.institution: Weizmann Institute of Science, Department of Physics of Complex Systems
bio-inspired.summary: The lab explicitly investigates biological computation at the protein and enzyme scale and describes enzymes as programmable viscoelastic materials. Its 2025 enzyme-mechanics study is a current mechanistic contribution to this programme.
bio-inspired.activity: The first-party publication list records the lab lead as coauthor on “Enzymes as viscoelastic catalytic machines,” Nature Physics 21(5), 787–798 (2025), and gives its mechanistic abstract. The same page also records a 2025 PNAS paper, though that speech-prosody work is not used to establish Bio fit.

bio-inspired.name: ELIXIR Lab
bio-inspired.institution: Toronto Metropolitan University
bio-inspired.summary: ELIXIR explicitly studies embodied damage recovery in reconfigurable robotics and bio-inspired shape-morphing soft robotics.
bio-inspired.activity: Current official portfolio lists active work on damage recovery and bio-inspired shape morphing.

bio-inspired.name: Elowitz Lab — Synthetic and Systems Biology
bio-inspired.institution: California Institute of Technology, Division of Biology and Biological Engineering
bio-inspired.summary: The current lab combines synthetic molecular-circuit construction with single-cell analysis to understand and program cellular sensing, response, memory, and cell-fate behaviors. Current 2026 outputs include engineered cell-decision mechanisms.
bio-inspired.activity: The lab-maintained publication page lists 2026 work on engineered caspase control and combinatorial integration of dopamine receptor signals. The official 2026 KITP schedule lists an Elowitz talk on synthetic circuits for programmable recognition and targeting.

bio-inspired.name: Embodied Cognitive Science Unit (ECSU)
bio-inspired.institution: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology (OIST)
bio-inspired.summary: ECSU conducts current research spanning origins of life and self-optimization, and explicitly uses computational modelling and artificial-life approaches. Current unit member Georgii Karelin studies artificial life/astrobiology, self-organization and enclosed ecosystem adaptation using nonlinear dynamics, cellular automata and agent-based models. This is relevant foundational modelling of life-like organization and adaptive living systems, but the unit is broadly embodied cognitive science and does not present itself as a dedicated biological-computation lab; relevance is therefore strongly related rather than core.
bio-inspired.activity: Current unit pages describe origins-of-life and self-optimization research using artificial life and computational models; the current team roster identifies Karelin as a doctoral candidate working on artificial life, astrobiology, self-organization and ecosystem adaptation. The unit publications page lists current 2026 outputs, including work coauthored by Froese and Karelin.

bio-inspired.name: Embrapa Synthetic Biology Laboratory (LBS)
bio-inspired.institution: Embrapa Genetic Resources and Biotechnology
bio-inspired.summary: Current LBS remit includes CRISPR- and synthetic-RNA-based biosensors, cell-free synthetic protein systems and synthetic-cell research. The bridge to molecular computation is inferred from molecular sensing and information processing; the current first-party programme does not claim logic gates or explicit computation.
bio-inspired.activity: Embrapa bibliography records the 2025 ACS Synthetic Biology article “Cell-free production of soybean leghemoglobins and nonsymbiotic hemoglobin” by current LBS researchers including Bittencourt and Rech. Current LBS and researcher pages identify the active unit and its biosensor/synthetic-cell remit.

bio-inspired.name: Emergence and Control in Development and Evolution (Archishman Raju)
bio-inspired.institution: National Centre for Biological Sciences, TIFR
bio-inspired.summary: Develops compact mathematical models of morphogenetic fields, Waddington landscapes, Turing patterns and developmental dynamics, including how development changes evolutionary trajectories.
bio-inspired.activity: NCBS 2024–25 annual report lists the lab's 2025 preprint on a Waddingtonian model of Turing-pattern dynamics and current work on developmental trajectories; current faculty page identifies the ongoing group program.

bio-inspired.name: EMERGENCE@ASU — Sara Imari Walker Lab
bio-inspired.institution: Arizona State University, Beyond Center for Fundamental Concepts in Science
topics: emergence of life from nonliving matter
bio-inspired.summary: The group develops theory and experiments to understand what life is and how life emerges from nonliving matter, including assembly theory as a measurable treatment of complexity, selection, and molecular organization. The current team page identifies Walker and active team members. This is an active origins-of-life mechanism programme, separate in identity from the broader Beyond Center.
bio-inspired.activity: The maintained lab homepage and team page currently describe the research programme and identify Walker as professor and team lead; the research page gives active work on assembly theory and origin-of-life transition mechanisms.

bio-inspired.name: Emerging Intelligent Substrates (EIS) Lab
bio-inspired.institution: Institute of Neuroinformatics, University of Zurich / ETH Zurich
topics: morphogenesis/self-organisation, neural cellular automata and repair
bio-inspired.summary: The EIS group’s current first-party remit explicitly investigates how intelligence emerges from physical substrates, studies brain structure-function across spatial/temporal scales, and uses silicon/resistive-memory devices to build intelligent systems. This is a specific biological/computational bridge in efficient physical computation and substrate-aware self-organization; it is not being counted because Gabriel Béna coauthored the paper alone. The current roster establishes him as a postdoc in Payvand’s group, while the lab itself has its own identity and programme. The ALIFE digital-circuit paper is not claimed as an EIS output.
bio-inspired.activity: Official current UZH/ETH roster lists Gabriel Béna as a postdoc in Payvand’s group; his current 2026 CV describes ongoing research in memristive substrates and modular computation. The official EIS page describes active group projects and methods.

bio-inspired.name: Emre Uğur Developmental Robotics Research Programme
bio-inspired.institution: Boğaziçi University
bio-inspired.summary: Uğur’s current program models developmental progress in robot sensorimotor learning and goal understanding. The source describes formation of a developmental-robotics group; this is recorded as a research programme, not a formal lab brand.
bio-inspired.activity: Current project page gives a 2025–2027 program; official profile confirms his present faculty role.

bio-inspired.name: Endothelial Cell Biology and Vascular Regeneration (Soumyashree Das)
bio-inspired.institution: National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS-TIFR)
bio-inspired.summary: The programme studies the cell and molecular mechanisms of vascular growth and remodeling, including developmental arterial patterning and tissue repair through vascular regeneration. It directly fits morphogenesis and repair.
bio-inspired.activity: The NCBS annual report 2024–25 describes ongoing arterial growth and regeneration work; the current lab publications page lists a 2026 preprint on cell-autonomous Wnt activity and endothelial reprogramming in coronary artery regeneration.

bio-inspired.name: Engineered and Experimental Evolution (E3) Lab
bio-inspired.institution: University of Michigan, Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology; Center for the Study of Complex Systems
bio-inspired.summary: The E3 Lab studies biological evolutionary mechanisms through paired computational and microbial experimental systems. Its current programme models host–parasite coevolution with populations of self-replicating digital organisms and investigates microbial host–virus evolution, directly connecting artificial life to biological evolution.
bio-inspired.activity: The 2025 ALIFE paper by E3 PI Luis Zaman and current E3 postdoc Matthew Andres Moreno develops phylogeny reconstruction methods for large digital-evolution simulations. A March 18, 2026 UMich MIDAS article documents Moreno’s active agent-based biological-evolution and lineage-tracking programme under Zaman and Dolson; UMich’s current CSCS directory lists Moreno in Zaman E3 Lab.

bio-inspired.name: Ennis Research Group – Solid-State Astrochemistry and Molecular Crystal Spectroscopy
bio-inspired.institution: University of Otago, Department of Chemistry
bio-inspired.summary: Laboratory astrochemistry examines molecular reactions and amino-acid precursor pathways in Titan-relevant ice/clathrate systems; the university explicitly frames the programme as investigating pathways toward life’s building blocks and Titan’s origin-of-life chemistry.
bio-inspired.activity: Current group site posted June 2026; Otago profile lists 2026 Titan-related papers; group carries ongoing Titan co-crystal research beyond the 2022–2024 Marsden award period.

bio-inspired.name: Epigenomics and Single Cell Biophysics Group
bio-inspired.institution: Radboud Institute for Molecular Life Sciences, Radboud University
bio-inspired.summary: The group studies specific epigenetic and metabolic mechanisms that let innate immune cells retain prior-stimulus history and alter later responses. Persistent lncRNA, chromatin and histone-lactylation states form a molecular cellular-memory mechanism, which is relevant by inference to basal cellular computation and learning. The connection is mechanistic and non-neural; the group does not claim to build AI or a computational device.
bio-inspired.activity: Radboudumc reported in 2025 on the Cell study “Long-term histone lactylation connects metabolic and epigenetic rewiring in innate immune memory,” including persistent histone marks and memory effects; the current Radboud group page lists Mhlanga as PI and a current team.

bio-inspired.name: Equipe ASTRO — Astrochimie, Spectroscopie, Théorie, Réactivité, Origines
bio-inspired.institution: PIIM, Aix-Marseille Université and CNRS
topics: laboratory simulation and quantum/dynamical chemical modeling
bio-inspired.summary: The ASTRO team has an explicit research axis on origin and emergence of prebiotic systems and studies how exogenous organic matter delivered to early Earth may contribute. The broad planetary-ice track qualifies only where the exact project connects to prebiotic systems; the presentation trails are classified individually.
bio-inspired.activity: Current ASTRO team page and filtered roster; official December 2025 origins-of-life activity identifies Danger as team head, and July 2026 official news documents current organic chemistry work relevant to life emergence.

bio-inspired.name: Eric Smith life-origin complex-systems programme
bio-inspired.institution: Earth-Life Science Institute (ELSI), Institute of Science Tokyo
bio-inspired.summary: ELSI currently lists him as a specially appointed professor; current first-party research evidence documents a computational chemical-evolution project and 2026 enzyme-evolution collaboration, addressing emergence and organization of life.
bio-inspired.activity: Current ELSI roster and SFI profile identify his roles/programme; dated Dec 2024 and Sep 2026 ELSI primary reports document computational chemistry and early metabolism work.

bio-inspired.name: Erzberger Group — Theory of Cellular and Multicellular Organisation
bio-inspired.institution: European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL)
bio-inspired.summary: Combines soft-matter and non-equilibrium physics with nonlinear dynamics to study how molecular signaling, cell mechanics and geometry generate self-organisation and embryo morphogenesis.
bio-inspired.activity: EMBL reported current 2026 work on how living cells process information through shape, boundaries and self-organisation; ERC GOAL runs 2026–2031.

bio-inspired.name: EvoChromo — Crucial Steps in Evolution: The Rise of Genome Architecture
bio-inspired.lead: Frédéric Berger (coordinator), Christa Schleper, and Florian Schur (shared project leadership)
bio-inspired.institution: University of Vienna; Gregor Mendel Institute for Molecular Plant Biology, Austrian Academy of Sciences; Institute of Science and Technology Austria
bio-inspired.summary: EvoChromo is a new decentralized lab asking when and how chromatin arose from prokaryotic building blocks and how its innovation contributed to cellular diversification and complex multicellular life. It combines archaeal biology, chromatin research, and structural biology across three Vienna research groups.
bio-inspired.activity: The official University of Vienna project page gives the active 1 September 2024–31 August 2029 project period. The ISTA partner page advertises a postdoctoral project specifically within the newly forming EvoChromo lab, with in-situ cryo-EM/cryo-ET methods.

bio-inspired.name: Evolutionary Adaptive System Laboratory

Its 2026 ALIFE output studies constructive evolutionary operations in molecular design, with controlled search and a measurable increase in discovered molecular scaffolds; the lab page also lists a current molecular-representation/ADMET research project. This is an active methodological programme in algorithmic scientific discovery.

The MIT Press article was published online 2026-08-17 and reports controlled experiments in molecular design (17 discovered macro-operations and 225 unique molecular scaffolds). Recent lab publications listed for 2025 corroborate active research. Current as of 2026-10-14.

Its remit explicitly spans evolutionary computation as both a model system for theory and a means to build better algorithms, making this a direct Bio-inspired evolution and artificial-life unit.
bio-inspired.activity: Current ECODE Lab roster lists Dolson as PI and several active research trainees. The 2025 ALIFE paper is a current lab-associated output on environmental connectivity and long-term evolutionary outcomes; the current lab describes digital evolutionary experiments and evolutionary-computation research.

bio-inspired.activity: University CV dated June 2026 lists recent evolutionary computation/robotics activity and current associate professorship.

bio-inspired.activity: Official lab news lists dated 2026 activity and current robotics work.

bio-inspired.name: Fei Sun Group — HKUST programmable gap-junction and multicellular communication programme
bio-inspired.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Department of Chemical and Biological Engineering
bio-inspired.summary: The PI-led lab develops protein-topology and chemo-optogenetic tools to control intercellular communication. Its 2025 CarGAP study reversibly switches gap-junction communication in vertebrate and invertebrate cells and examines cell-cell signal transfer in a Drosophila stem-cell niche. This is a mechanistic programme on multicellular cellular coordination, with an inferred connection to collective-cell information processing. The sources do not claim cognitive computation, and inclusion is limited to this mechanism rather than the lab’s broad biomaterials portfolio.

The paper reports reversible chemogenetic/optogenetic control of gap junctions and cell-to-cell chemical/electrical signaling, including cAMP transfer within Drosophila germline stem-cell-niche interactions. Current group and HKUST profiles identify Fei Sun as active PI and Professor.

bio-inspired.lead: José Antonio Manzanares Andreu (director); Javier Cervera Montesinos (member)
bio-inspired.institution: Universitat de València, Department of Earth Physics and Thermodynamics
bio-inspired.summary: Official team description combines cellular/multicellular bioelectricity modeling (including instructive development and regeneration patterns) with biomimetic nanopores performing information-processing and simple logic functions. The current unit is FET-TRANS, not an individual lab inferred from coauthorship.
bio-inspired.activity: The university team directory names the director and current members, explicitly lists its two relevant research lines, and university records show Cervera’s 2026 papers on multicellular bioelectric regionalization and learning in ionic nanofluidic pores.

bio-inspired.name: FinalSpark

bio-inspired.activity: Page copyright 2014-2024 and a customer statement about testing bio-inspired robotic perception algorithms directly on biological organoids.

bio-inspired.name: Flowers AI & CogSci Lab
bio-inspired.institution: Inria Centre; University of Bordeaux; ENSTA Paris
bio-inspired.summary: FLOWERS’ current CARL project applies goal-conditioned autotelic reinforcement learning to discover and control life-like self-organizing solitons in Lenia. The primary ALIFE method uses closed-loop local interventions to discover stable patterns, steer them, and generalize across rules and initial states. This is a concrete digital artificial-life and emergence-method programme; it does not establish biological origins or self-replication. The unit already exists as R0146, so this is a current-method/activity evidence update rather than a new identity.
bio-inspired.activity: Official FLOWERS project listings through 2026 include cellular-automata emergence/control and artificial-life pattern projects; the exact CARL paper/companion page documents the current method and lists the ALIFE 2026 publication.

bio-inspired.name: Francis Corson Developmental Self-Organization Programme
bio-inspired.institution: Laboratoire de Physique de l’École Normale Supérieure (LPENS), ENS-PSL/CNRS
bio-inspired.summary: Corson develops theory and quantitative modeling of patterning and morphogenesis, with current projects in Drosophila neural patterning and amniote embryo development. A 2024 paper directly demonstrates mechanically mediated embryo self-organization and regulation.

Current ENS profile and group page identify his programme and topics.

bio-inspired.name: Frontier Computing

bio-inspired.name: Hiroki Kojima — Life & Information research programme (SDS/Henkaku)
bio-inspired.institution: School of Design & Science, Chiba Institute of Technology; Henkaku Center
bio-inspired.summary: Kojima’s current first-party faculty profile explicitly includes continuous cellular automaton Lenia and artificial-life/biological-life hybrid systems in his research remit. The Bio fit is strongly related to the self-organization/artificial-life theme; the listed Tetrahymena work is not presented as cellular computation or collective cell intelligence.

bio-inspired.name: Hiroyuki Iizuka Artificial Life, AI & Complex Systems Programme

These current lines map to neural/self-organisation and developmental computation, without evidence of morphogenesis or body–brain co-design.

bio-inspired.activity: Stanford profile confirms faculty and Arc appointments from 2024 onward and current advisees/courses; a recent institutional interview documents the lab’s active development of cell tracking and control methods.

The current programme explicitly studies intracellular flows in developmental processes, ciliary transport, flagellar mechanics and collective dynamics; this is a mechanistic bridge to developmental self-organisation, not a generic soft-matter inclusion.
bio-inspired.activity: The current group page lists 2026 papers on bacterial aerotaxis and collective sperm dynamics and identifies current group members.

bio-inspired.name: Living Machines Lab
bio-inspired.institution: Østfold University College
bio-inspired.summary: Uses neural cellular automata as models of biological development, regeneration and ageing, and studies collective learning and agency in multi-agent ecosystems.
bio-inspired.activity: 2026 paper studies self-replicating neural cellular automata, emergent phenotype/genotype diversity and self-maintenance.

bio-inspired.name: Living Matter Lab — Ignacio Bordeu
bio-inspired.institution: Department of Physics, Faculty of Physical and Mathematical Sciences, Universidad de Chile
bio-inspired.summary: The lab explicitly studies how mechanical forces and chemical signals let cells and microorganisms self-organize into biological structures, including tissue morphogenesis and adaptive transport networks. A current 2026 Fondecyt project combines theory and experiments to study the growth and organization of biological fluid networks and Physarum. The programme is retained on this direct mechanistic basis.
bio-inspired.activity: Official 2026 Fondecyt Regular project announcement names Bordeu as PI and details ongoing theory-plus-experiment research on biological flow-network organization and Physarum; current UChile faculty roster independently supports his active appointment.
