bio-inspired.name: Lu Hui DNA Computing Group
bio-inspired.institution: Shanghai University, Institute of Materials Biology
bio-inspired.summary: DNA computing group designs molecular circuits and signal-transmission systems; current work includes programmable DNA computing for intelligent nucleic-acid analysis.
bio-inspired.activity: Shanghai University profile reports current appointment since February 2025 and principal-investigator NSFC grant active 2026–2030.

bio-inspired.name: Lulu Qian Lab — Molecular Programming and DNA Computation
bio-inspired.institution: California Institute of Technology
bio-inspired.summary: The Qian lab designs biochemical systems that process information and learn. In 2025 it reported a supervised-learning DNA neural network and heat-rechargeable computation in DNA logic and neural networks.
bio-inspired.activity: Caltech reported on 3 September 2025 that the Qian lab built a DNA neural network that learns from examples; the lab publication page lists two 2025 Nature papers on supervised learning and heat-rechargeable computation.

bio-inspired.name: Lung Repair and Plasticity Lab
bio-inspired.institution: Institute for Stem Cell Science and Regenerative Medicine (inStem)
bio-inspired.summary: The current lab studies developmental epithelial plasticity, tissue-state remodelling and lung repair after injury using Drosophila, mouse and human lung systems. These biological mechanisms map directly to the scope’s repair/developmental themes; an engineered-computation bridge is inferred.
bio-inspired.activity: The lab website lists ongoing developmental-plasticity and repair projects, and the institute published a March 2026 PI-led study/release; institute recruiting notices for Guha’s lab also appear in 2026.

bio-inspired.name: Maikel Rheinstädter Research Group — Prebiotic Polymer Formation
bio-inspired.institution: McMaster University, Department of Physics & Astronomy
bio-inspired.summary: The group experimentally and computationally studies how abiotic environmental cycles can generate complex biological polymers. Its current work uses controlled wet–dry cycling and an environmental simulator to test how RNA-like polymers form from simple precursors under early-Earth conditions.
bio-inspired.activity: Scientific Reports published the group’s 2026 work on abiotic formation of RNase-resistant phosphodiester and pyrophosphate-linked polymers via controlled wet–dry cycling (online 2026-06-13; version of record 2026-08-27). Rheinstädter is a corresponding author and led conceptualization, funding, investigation, methodology and supervision.

bio-inspired.name: Malcolm Heywood evolutionary-computation research programme
bio-inspired.institution: Dalhousie University, Faculty of Computer Science
bio-inspired.summary: Heywood’s current researcher programme develops genetic programming, co-evolution and reinforcement learning methods; the 2025 GECCO output applies evolutionary control to Braitenberg-style navigation. The adjacent Network Information Management and Security (NIMS) group is not counted as a bio-inspired lab.
bio-inspired.activity: Current faculty unit and 2025 current GECCO output substantiate the program; Bayer and Smith remain source-limited as to membership.

bio-inspired.name: Manning Group — collective tissue behaviour and morphogenesis
bio-inspired.institution: Syracuse University, Department of Physics
bio-inspired.summary: The PI-led group studies cell collectives, organogenesis, and tissue mechanics; its current 2025–2026 work measures how collective forces and mechanical properties pattern and shape developing tissues.
bio-inspired.activity: Current group bibliography lists 2025–2026 work on embryonic organ morphology, epithelial morphogenesis, epithelial tissue mechanics, and active physical learning; current PI and group roster are on the people page.

bio-inspired.name: Marko Popović Research Group — Morphogenesis and Regeneration
bio-inspired.institution: Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems; Ruđer Bošković Institute
bio-inspired.summary: The current programme studies how living tissues fold, flow, regenerate and self-organize, including Hydra body-axis formation and active tissue mechanics.
bio-inspired.activity: Current 2025–2026 lab publications include Hydra regeneration, tissue-folding, order/disorder during development and cell-division mechanics; official RBI profile confirms current senior research appointment.

bio-inspired.name: Marshall Lab — single-cell learning, cell geometry and regeneration
bio-inspired.institution: University of California, San Francisco, Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics
bio-inspired.summary: The current Marshall Lab studies single-cell patterning and regeneration; its 2026 Stentor work demonstrates habituation without neurons and identifies a molecular signalling mechanism. This directly fits Bio themes 2 and 5.
bio-inspired.activity: UCSF reported April 2026 Current Biology findings from the Marshall Lab on Stentor habituation, calcium/CaMKII signalling and protein modification. The current UCSF faculty page links the Marshall Lab and describes its Stentor pattern formation and regeneration programme.

bio-inspired.name: Martin Falk — AI-guided Search for Programmable Materials
bio-inspired.institution: Eric and Wendy Schmidt AI in Science programme, University of Chicago Data Science Institute
bio-inspired.summary: Falk’s funded fellowship programme aims to find materials that compute, morph and adapt by combining active learning, computer vision and AI-guided search of fabrication/control spaces. Current official sources establish this research aim and fellowship identity; earlier materials-adaptation work supports the underlying methods. The record does not claim that autonomous AI discovery outputs or a 2027 faculty lab already exist.
bio-inspired.activity: Current DSI profile identifies him as an Eric and Wendy Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellow and describes his active AI-agent and active-learning project for computational, morphing and adaptive materials.

bio-inspired.name: María Sofía Urbieta — DYNALIFE small-RNA origins-of-life programme at CINDEFI
bio-inspired.institution: CINDEFI, CONICET–Universidad Nacional de La Plata
bio-inspired.summary: Current work explicitly seeks minimal self-replicating RNAs in Earth-analog extreme environments to investigate prebiotic entities and origins of life. Field sampling, sequencing and metatranscriptomic/bioinformatic analysis supply the substantive experimental programme.
bio-inspired.activity: CONICET La Plata reports two field campaigns conducted in March 2026 and ongoing processing/study of collected samples in Urbieta’s CINDEFI laboratory.

bio-inspired.name: Massimiliano Esposito — Complex Systems and Statistical Mechanics
bio-inspired.institution: University of Luxembourg, Department of Physics and Materials Science
bio-inspired.summary: Group develops nonequilibrium thermodynamics for biological/chemical energy-information flows, including metabolic transduction, self-replication and noise-driven information processing.
bio-inspired.activity: 2025 graduate theses include free-energy transduction in chemical reaction networks and nonequilibrium thermodynamics of growth supervised by Esposito.

bio-inspired.name: Mathematical and Applied Visual Computing Group (MAVC)
bio-inspired.institution: Technical University of Darmstadt; Fraunhofer IGD
bio-inspired.summary: MAVC currently supervises NCA projects in video segmentation, continual learning and simulation. These are computational NCA applications; no biological motivation is inferred.
bio-inspired.activity: Official profile lists several 2026 NCA theses; department confirms his MAVC chair.

bio-inspired.name: Mathis Group (Cole Mathis)
bio-inspired.institution: Arizona State University, School of Complex Adaptive Systems and Biodesign Center for Biocomputing, Security and Society
bio-inspired.summary: The Mathis Group models how life-like organization can emerge from simpler non-living components using simulation and statistical methods. Its AlChemy programme studies artificial chemistry as an artificial-life model and current work extends simulation, visualization, prebiotic-chemistry comparisons and spatial organization. The 2025 proceedings paper shows endogenous selection of functions within lambda-calculus chemistry; this is a direct artificial-life/chemical-evolution mechanism programme, not generic AI or ordinary chemistry.
bio-inspired.activity: The official 2025–2027 “Visualizing AlChemy” project under Mathis Group states that the group has reimplemented AlChemy and plans continuing simulations, analyses, visualizations, prebiotic-chemistry comparisons and model extensions. Mathis Group’s current publication page lists the 2025 ALIFE paper and current 2026 work by Devansh Vimal and Cole Mathis; official ASU profile confirms Mathis as a current assistant professor and researcher in the living-origins boundary.

bio-inspired.name: Matsuura Laboratory
bio-inspired.institution: Earth-Life Science Institute (ELSI), Institute of Science Tokyo
bio-inspired.summary: A current ELSI PI-led laboratory develops molecular and artificial-cell systems, explicitly aims for self-replication, and bridges prebiotic organization with synthetic life. This is a direct mechanistic “what is life?” programme.
bio-inspired.activity: Lab homepage records new papers on 2026-05-25 and 2026-04-27, a renewed member list on 2026-04-27, and active researchers/students.

bio-inspired.name: Matter Lab — Aspuru-Guzik and Bernales Group
bio-inspired.institution: University of Toronto
bio-inspired.summary: The group page explicitly describes closed-loop laboratories joining ML, robotics, computer vision and automated characterization to accelerate materials discovery.
bio-inspired.activity: The maintained group publication list names September2026 La Agente Óptima and August2026 MoSeS autonomous chromatography work, and 2025 El Agente and ORGANA robotic chemistry studies. The current group roster explicitly names both principal investigators.

bio-inspired.name: Matthew Egbert origin-of-life and sensorimotor agency research programme
bio-inspired.institution: University of Auckland, Faculty of Science
bio-inspired.summary: Egbert’s current programme builds computational models of living systems, including origins-of-life metabolism and self-maintaining sensorimotor habits; a 2026 funded collaboration studies agency emerging in living systems. Its connection to self-organization is explicit in his model description; mapping that work to the published morphogenesis/self-organization page theme is an inference.
bio-inspired.activity: University of Auckland news dated 2026-08-31 reports Egbert’s role in a funded three-year international institute studying agency and intelligence in living systems; current profile describes computational research on origins of life, self-maintaining sensorimotor patterns and evolutionary robotics.

bio-inspired.name: Matthew Pasek — Origins-of-Life Phosphorus Chemistry Programme
bio-inspired.institution: Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences
bio-inspired.summary: Pasek investigates origin-of-life chemistry from geology and planetary science with a specialization in phosphorus redox chemistry, including plausible prebiotic phosphate alternatives.
bio-inspired.activity: Pasek investigates origin-of-life chemistry from geology and planetary science with a specialization in phosphorus redox chemistry, including plausible prebiotic phosphate alternatives.

bio-inspired.name: McNamara Lab — Synthetic Developmental Biology
bio-inspired.institution: Yale University, Department of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology; Wu Tsai Institute
bio-inspired.summary: The lab uses stem-cell organoids and embryo models as experimental systems for multicellular self-organization, then programs genetic circuits to read and write signaling interactions. It tests whether observed signals predict cell fate and uses perturbations to test theoretical models of developmental pattern formation.
bio-inspired.activity: Yale’s current Wu Tsai faculty profile identifies McNamara as Assistant Professor and Investigator, states he joined Yale in January 2025, and lists related institute updates through September 2026. Yale’s PEB page lists a current student in the McNamara lab; the lab page documents ongoing experimental methods and programme.

bio-inspired.activity: Official MPI-CBG current group listing and research-focus page identify Huch’s active organoid, regeneration, and disease-mechanism lab; page reports a 2025 human liver-model news item.

bio-inspired.name: Meroz Lab — Physics of Plant Computational and Behavioral Processes
bio-inspired.institution: Tel Aviv University
bio-inspired.summary: Studies plants as distributed information-processing organisms, including collective shade avoidance, local sensing, plant memory and self-organized growth responses.
bio-inspired.activity: 2024–2026 papers and official TAU reporting document collective plant self-organization, 2025 plant force-measurement work and a 2026 PNAS study of decentralized plant sensory integration.

bio-inspired.name: Michael Dunn — Rhizobial Polyamine Sensing Programme
bio-inspired.institution: Centro de Ciencias Genómicas, Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México (UNAM)
bio-inspired.summary: The group studies a bacterial chemosensory mechanism: specific extracellular polyamines are detected by NspS/MbaA, transduced through a c-di-GMP second-messenger pathway, and change biofilm, exopolysaccharide, aggregation and motility phenotypes. This gives an explicit molecular signal-processing chain with community-scale outcomes. Its connection to basal cognition or cellular computation is an inferred mechanistic bridge; the record does not claim cognition, an engineered computing device, or that all rhizobial metabolism is in scope.
bio-inspired.activity: The current CCG profile lists this as Dunn’s current research objective; a dedicated UNAM project on transport/perception of environmental polyamines ran 2023–2025. The group’s 2023 experimentally tested NspS-MbaA paper establishes the signal-processing mechanism. CCG lists a separate 2025 publication for current programme activity, though that paper concerns transporter-mediated antimicrobial resistance/symbiosis, not the signal system itself.

bio-inspired.name: Michael Levy Lab — Biophysical Systems Toward Artificial Living Matter
bio-inspired.institution: Technion – Israel Institute of Technology
bio-inspired.summary: Builds DNA-chip and cell-free gene-expression platforms to reconstitute cellular processes and pursue autonomous self-replicating artificial cells.
bio-inspired.activity: Current lab page lists three active projects (surface-bound artificial cell, membrane division, biolab-on-chip) and recruiting; independent current lab identity confirmed.

bio-inspired.activity: Current Mainz institutional appointment and recruitment; personal site lists2026 Artificial Intelligence and Intelligent Matter and2026 active-matter review.

bio-inspired.name: Miguel Aguilera's nonequilibrium neural-computation program (BCAM MCEN)
bio-inspired.institution: Basque Center for Applied Mathematics (BCAM), Mathematical, Computational and Experimental Neuroscience (MCEN)
bio-inspired.summary: Aguilera develops mechanistic nonequilibrium models of neural systems, including associative memory networks, with explicit thermodynamic measures of entropy production/dissipation and links to information processing, learning and memory. The ALIFE 2025 paper extends this to continuous-time recurrent neural networks.
bio-inspired.activity: BCAM lists Aguilera as a current Ikerbasque and Ramón y Cajal fellow in MCEN and an ongoing HOLISM project. Its research page explicitly treats entropy dissipation as a signature/limit of associative memory and cites the 2025 ALIFE work; the 2025 paper models nonequilibrium thermodynamics of associative-memory CTRNNs.

bio-inspired.name: Miki Ebisuya Group
bio-inspired.institution: TU Dresden, Cluster of Excellence Physics of Life (PoL), Dresden

bio-inspired.activity: Official PoL 2026 report names Ebisuya as current group leader and reports self-organizing bovine tissues from embryonic stem cells.

bio-inspired.name: Ming & Sato Laboratory — bio-inspired locomotion and robots
bio-inspired.institution: The University of Electro-Communications, Cluster II / Department of Mechanical and Intelligent Systems Engineering
bio-inspired.summary: The programme co-designs robot morphology, compliant muscle-tendon mechanisms, and control using animal musculoskeletal and neural-motor principles. Its 2025 quadruped paper evaluates elastic-force-feedback CPG gait control, and an active 2024–2027 project studies whole-body muscle-tendon networks. This is a direct body–brain co-design bridge; the group’s directory wording about evolving robots is not treated as proof of evolutionary-algorithm work.
bio-inspired.activity: The official UEC profile lists a current 2024–2027 PI project on whole-body muscle-tendon networks for agile locomotion and a 2025 paper, “Experimental Evaluation of Elastic Force Feedback CPG-based Gait Controller on a Bio-inspired Quadruped Robot.” The page also lists 2024–2026 related locomotion and fish-robot activity.

bio-inspired.name: Mitsuharu Matsumoto Laboratory
bio-inspired.institution: The University of Electro-Communications, Department of Informatics
bio-inspired.summary: The lab studies how biological self-organization and replication can inform robotic manufacturing and systems. Its 2026 self-repairing robot work and explicitly described self-organization programme support a direct mechanism bridge to the self-organization/repair theme. The evidence concerns engineering systems, not biological morphogenesis experiments.
bio-inspired.activity: The current lab publication list includes a 2026 accepted necrophagy-inspired self-repairing robot paper and 2025 work on plant-growth robot bridges and environment-assembled robot exteriors. The member page identifies Matsumoto as an Associate Professor and lists current students.

bio-inspired.name: Mizuki Oka — Artificial Life and Open-Ended Algorithms Programme, Chiba Tech SDS / Henkaku Center
bio-inspired.institution: Chiba Institute of Technology, Graduate School of Design & Science; Henkaku Center

This is the continuation of the same PI-led identity previously represented by Oka Laboratory at Tsukuba, now institutionally at Chiba Tech SDS/Henkaku Center. It remains distinct from the separately incorporated Artificial Life Institute, where Oka holds a concurrent leadership role.
bio-inspired.activity: Current Chiba Tech faculty page lists Oka as Professor and Department Head / Engineer of Artificial Life and describes current open-ended algorithm and ALife research and active intelligent-agent teaching/research supervision. Current Henkaku Center roster lists her as Dean.

bio-inspired.name: Molecular Evolution, RNA World and Biosensors Group
bio-inspired.institution: Centro de Astrobiología (CSIC-INTA)
bio-inspired.summary: A current CAB PI-led group studies origin and early evolution of life through experimental and theoretical RNA-world/prebiotic chemistry and in-vitro molecular evolution. These methods directly address life emergence and molecular replication.
bio-inspired.activity: CAB identifies Briones as staff researcher and current group coordinator, names current origin-of-life/RNA-world and prebiotic-chemistry research, and states he coordinates the CSIC Origins of Life interdisciplinary platform.

bio-inspired.name: Molecular Programming Group (Christopher Thachuk)

bio-inspired.activity: Own site verifies current UW appointment and ongoing DNA computing/molecular programming research, including explicit DNA information-processing circuits and chemical reaction network computation.

bio-inspired.name: Molecular Programming Group (KTH)
bio-inspired.institution: KTH Royal Institute of Technology
bio-inspired.summary: Current group builds molecular-programming tools and DNA-based information-processing systems.
bio-inspired.activity: Official group site lists 2026 molecular-programming software, grants, new students and lab activity.

bio-inspired.activity: Tohoku Engineering news dated 2026-10-07 reports a two-wavelength system controlling mRNA synthesis and cleavage inside artificial cells; university page identifies Nomura as the current lead.

Its current described methods include nucleic-acid liquid-crystal phases and templated polymerization, directly matching the scheduled RNA polymerization and selection work.
bio-inspired.activity: Current SAM Lab page identifies Fraccia as the PI building the research team, gives current programme themes and lists current coacervate-protocell and nucleic-acid self-assembly research; LBE research page links the SAM team.

bio-inspired.institution: Institute of Chemistry, Hebrew University of Jerusalem

bio-inspired.activity: Current official group page lists recruitment and research on chemical evolution; current team page names Frenkel-Pinter as PI and identifies the ongoing proto-peptide origins programme.

bio-inspired.name: Morphogenesis and Cellular Dynamics (Shimmi Lab)
bio-inspired.institution: University of Helsinki, Institute of Biotechnology / HiLIFE
bio-inspired.summary: Studies how spatial signaling, cell-shape changes, and cellular communication coordinate Drosophila tissue patterning and 3D morphogenesis. Its connection to computational/developmental systems is an inference from an explicit morphogen-patterning mechanism; the scope is limited to that current morphogenesis group, not all developmental biology.

bio-inspired.name: Morphogenesis Lab, IISER Kolkata
bio-inspired.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Kolkata, Department of Biological Sciences
bio-inspired.summary: The lab uses Drosophila genetics and live-cell imaging to study how intercellular communication and coordinated cell behaviour produce cell-fate changes, epithelial shape transformations, group migration and developmental morphogenesis. 2025 work documents multi-cell epithelial phagocytosis and microtubule membrane nanotubes that transport vesicles during egg morphogenesis. The biological mechanism is explicit; the bridge to computational or bio-inspired collective architectures is inferred.
bio-inspired.activity: The May 2025 JCB article identifies Prasad as corresponding author with supervision, funding acquisition and project administration and shows a 4–5 cell collective mechanism in developmental nurse-cell clearance. The linked PLOS Biology 2025 paper examines vesicle transport through membrane nanotubes during micropyle morphogenesis. The official Autumn 2025 IISER course lists Prasad and current morphology/regeneration topics; lab page lists current fellows.

Its current roster includes Josh Bongard and PhD student Nate Gaylinn, both authors of this ADJACENT ALIFE paper. The paper’s simulated HNCA intervention search is an author trail, not a new lab or proof that all current MECLab work uses neural cellular automata.

The 2025 ALIFE session lists the paper authors.

bio-inspired.name: Morsut Lab

bio-inspired.activity: USC lists new 2026–31 PI funding and 2026 publications on kidney-organoid patterning and cell-cell interactomes; July 2026 lab report documents synthetic organizer cells.

This is a computational artificial-life/self-organization programme. The exact paper demonstrates self-organized weight growth and architectural generalization; it does not demonstrate organismal self-replication, open-ended evolution or biological life origins.
bio-inspired.activity: Current company project page and company-owned code repository document MetaNCA; paper accepted to ALIFE 2026. The company page identifies current founders Meet Barot and Daniel Berenberg.

bio-inspired.name: Nathaniel Virgo — artificial-life, origins-of-life and agenthood research programme
bio-inspired.institution: University of Hertfordshire, Centre of Data Innovation Research / Department of Physics, Astronomy and Mathematics
bio-inspired.summary: Hertfordshire’s current researcher profile confirms Virgo’s current identity and research interests in artificial life, statistical mechanics, evolutionary theory and origins of life. His first-party current research agenda asks how goal-directedness emerges, how evolution itself evolves, and how chemical systems develop cellular complexity, addressed with mathematical/computational methods. A 2026 paper with Martin Biehl formalizes chemistry-like species and reactions in general dynamical systems, using Game of Life gliders as an example. This is an active artificial-life and artificial-chemistry programme; its connection to the scope’s self-organisation/cellular-molecular computation themes is an inference, so retain STRONGLY_RELATED rather than CORE. The unit is a researcher-led programme at Hertfordshire, not an independent branded lab.
bio-inspired.activity: U Hertfordshire’s current profile identifies Virgo in its Centre of Data Innovation Research and lists artificial life, statistical mechanics, evolution and origin-of-life interests. His first-party homepage describes current work on evolvability and chemical systems becoming cell-like. In July 2026 he coauthored “Towards chemistries in dynamical systems,” accepted for presentation at ALIFE 2026, formalizing chemistry-like descriptions of dynamical systems and Game of Life gliders.

Le Goff’s current generative design project belongs to this shared programme for this denominator; Sarah Thomson is a related author whose own current programme is broader fitness-landscape analysis.

UCL reported new experimental work in 2025 on joining RNA and amino acids under early-Earth conditions.
bio-inspired.activity: UCL’s 27 August 2025 report names Powner as senior author and states the experiment linked RNA with amino acids in conditions plausibly present on early Earth; the current lab page identifies its active chemical origins programme and research remit.

bio-inspired.name: Prebiotic Chemistry in Exoplanet Environments
bio-inspired.institution: Center for Space and Habitability, University of Bern
bio-inspired.summary: Current PI-led project uses coupled climate-chemistry models to evaluate atmospheric production and delivery of prebiotic precursors on exoplanets; current research also models photochemical shielding of prebiotic compounds.
bio-inspired.activity: Official CSH page states project start 1 October 2026, names Braam as lead, and describes current SNSF funding; researcher publication page lists 2026 prebiotic shielding paper.

bio-inspired.name: Priesemann Research Group / Complex Systems Theory
bio-inspired.institution: Max Planck Institute for Dynamics and Self-Organization
bio-inspired.summary: The group studies self-organized learning in neural networks to derive robust and energy-efficient compute principles for AI, including infomorphic networks.

bio-inspired.name: Principles of Biomolecular Systems (Thomas E. Ouldridge)
bio-inspired.institution: Imperial College London, Department of Bioengineering
bio-inspired.summary: Models biochemical sensing, copying and self-assembly as information-processing systems, deriving thermodynamic costs and limits for molecular computation.
bio-inspired.activity: Imperial Engineering Biology centre lists the current Principles of Biomolecular Systems group; the group page is its official current canonical URL. The old /people/.../research-group URL returned 404.

bio-inspired.name: Probing Origin of Life Possibilities, Atmospheric Redox, & Terrestrial Environment Evolution (NASA ICAR)
bio-inspired.institution: Purdue University-led interdisciplinary team
bio-inspired.summary: A current five-year NASA programme explicitly studies whether early Mars environments were favorable for the origin of life, combining mission and meteorite data, Earth analog fieldwork, geochemical and climate models, and lab experiments. Purdue independently describes Olson’s active faculty programme in climate/biogeochemical modelling of life–environment coevolution, planetary habitability and life detection. This is origins-context research, not a lab reconstructing life’s emergence at molecular scale.
bio-inspired.activity: NASA’s current 2024 ICAR page lists the selected five-year team and question. A March 2026 NASA Postdoctoral Program opportunity calls for fellows on the same named project and provides current advisors, supporting ongoing funded activity; Purdue’s current faculty page describes Olson’s group and methods.

bio-inspired.name: Process Optimization & Control Laboratory — DNA Computing and Diagnosis
bio-inspired.institution: Indian Institute of Technology Delhi
bio-inspired.summary: The current lab explicitly lists DNA computing and diagnosis; its 2025 paper demonstrates logic-gate computation through methylation-dependent DNA oligomer structure and electrical impedance output.
bio-inspired.activity: The lab’s current research listing includes DNA Computing and Diagnosis; its publication page lists 2025–26 research, including the 2025 DNA logic-circuit experiment coauthored by Ramteke.

bio-inspired.name: Protocell Models Group — Ning Gao
bio-inspired.institution: School of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Beijing Institute of Technology
bio-inspired.summary: Gao’s independent research group constructs protocell models from designed amphiphiles and colloidal particles to study cellular nonlinear transformations of matter, information and energy. This is a specific experimental model programme in protocellular organization, not generic materials chemistry.
bio-inspired.activity: Official BIT profile states Gao joined in March 2023 and remains an independent PI, describes the current group research direction and recruitment for doctoral/postdoctoral researchers.

bio-inspired.name: Protopolis Lab
bio-inspired.institution: NYU Shanghai
bio-inspired.summary: The current lab explicitly studies governance and coordination when decentralized AI agents act with increasing autonomy; it coauthored an ALIFE case study of an open-ended, real-world agent-evolution experiment. The link to Bio open-endedness is inferred from that concrete project, while the lab’s stated programme is governance and collective life rather than evolutionary-algorithm development.
bio-inspired.activity: The lab page lists current agentic-system research and NYU profile lists 2025 ALIFE coauthored output plus 2026 CHI Protocol Futuring; direct NYU page open timed out but full current official page content was returned by indexed search.

bio-inspired.name: Quantiphi Phi Labs — Applied Research, Life Sciences (EPOSMol programme)
bio-inspired.institution: Quantiphi Phi Labs, Applied Research — Life Sciences
bio-inspired.summary: Quantiphi’s Applied Research—Life Sciences programme developed EPOSMol, an evolutionary policy-gradient framework that searches molecular latent space for drug leads. The mechanism directly links evolutionary computation to automated discovery, which is an explicit Bio-inspired theme. Molecules are the design target; the evidence does not claim DNA/cellular computation or biologically inspired molecular mechanisms.
bio-inspired.activity: Quantiphi’s current corporate research page describes Phi Labs as its R&D hub and records continuing breakthrough research through 2025; its 2026 corporate post continues to promote EPOSMol as an active molecular-design framework. The authors’ 2025 ICLR workshop paper names Quantiphi Applied Research—Life Sciences and documents the method and experiments.

bio-inspired.name: Quantitative Cell Biology Lab (Shaon Chakrabarti)
bio-inspired.institution: National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS-TIFR)
bio-inspired.summary: The lab studies single-cell decision/fate dynamics and how heterogeneous cells produce population behavior, combining experiments with statistical and computational models. This is a specific biological information-processing/decision mechanism, relevant to the scope’s basal cognition and collective-cell decision theme; the bridge to engineered computation is inferred, and no claim of cellular consciousness is made.
bio-inspired.activity: A 2025 iScience paper models circadian control of cell proliferation using stochastic simulations and single-cell lineage data; current NCBS PI page and research page describe the active lab programme and recruitment.

bio-inspired.name: Rafael Peña Miller Programme — bacterial adaptation and cellular phenotypic heterogeneity
bio-inspired.institution: Centro de Ciencias Genómicas, Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México (UNAM), Systems Biology Program
bio-inspired.summary: The current PI-led programme combines mathematical models, simulations, microfluidics and experimental evolution to study how bacteria adapt to complex environments and how gene-regulatory interactions shape antibiotic responses and phenotypic heterogeneity among genetically identical cells. The cellular-computation bridge is an inference: the work investigates how molecular regulatory mechanisms encode and vary adaptive cellular responses. It is not presented as an AI programme or as origin-of-life research.
bio-inspired.activity: The current official CCG profile identifies Peña-Miller as a permanent full-time Systems Biology investigator and lists four 2026 publications, including conditional filamentation and bacterial survival in toxic environments, plasmid mutation rates, antibiotic response and plasmid community stability.

bio-inspired.name: Raffaele Saladino prebiotic molecular-evolution programme
bio-inspired.institution: Department of Chemistry and Drug Technologies, Sapienza University of Rome
bio-inspired.summary: Current professor-led programme in synthesis and molecular evolution relevant to prebiotic chemistry, with current 2026 work on peptide and PNA-component synthesis.
bio-inspired.activity: Current Sapienza professor profile lists 2026 prebiotic synthesis and molecular-evolution outputs.

bio-inspired.name: RahmLab — Martin Rahm
bio-inspired.institution: Chalmers University of Technology
bio-inspired.summary: The group uses quantum-chemical and computational methods to model prebiotic reactions and chemical systems relevant to the emergence of life; a current funded project explicitly studies predicted prebiotic origins of polypeptides.
bio-inspired.activity: Chalmers lists the active 2025–2028 Swedish Research Council project “Predicting Prebiotic Origins of Polypeptides and Solid-State Chemistry on Titan” and 2026 prebiotic-chemistry publications.

bio-inspired.name: Raj Ladher Lab — inner-ear morphogenesis and cellular patterning
bio-inspired.institution: National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS-TIFR)
bio-inspired.summary: The lab investigates how embryonic signals coordinate cell identity, patterning, force and tissue shape to build the inner ear. This is a direct morphogenesis mechanism within the stated Bio scope; no engineering prototype is implied.
bio-inspired.activity: NCBS research report dated 10 September 2025 covers current group findings on cellular organization/orientation in inner-ear development; current course page records Ladher teaching Development Biology in Aug–Nov 2025.

bio-inspired.name: Randall D. Beer — dynamical and computational biology research programme
bio-inspired.institution: Indiana University Bloomington, Cognitive Science Program; Program in Neuroscience; Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering
bio-inspired.summary: Beer’s current dynamical biology programme includes recent work on cellular viability: mapping how subcellular and cell-network states cross life-death constraints, including coupled cellular systems. The direct mechanism concerns cellular agency and survival rather than an explicit computational or cognitive process. Its connection to basal cognition and collective-cell intelligence is an inference based on the programme’s treatment of cellular state, behavioral viability and inter-cell coupling as organized agential dynamics.
bio-inspired.activity: The 2026 peer-reviewed paper “Matters of life and death in computational cell biology” by McShaffrey, Agmon and Beer develops cell-viability theory; the current programme page lists the 2025 ALIFE viability paper and 2026 outputs. IU faculty sources corroborate Beer’s current role and ongoing dynamical/computational biology remit.

bio-inspired.name: Reality Design Lab — Wild Agents open-ended artificial life programme

The Spore.fun case describes on-chain agents spawning, competing and reproducing with mutation and externally determined selection; Hu is currently presenting this programme at the ALIFE 2026 workshop. This is an explicit open-ended artificial-life mechanism, not merely general alignment or human–AI interaction.
bio-inspired.activity: Current 2026 ALIFE workshop programme lists Botao Amber Hu as invited speaker for “Artificial life in the wild,” identifies the talk as part of the Wild Agents project, and describes Spore in the Wild as an open-ended-evolution experiment. bio-inspired.name: Red Interdisciplinaria de Autoorganización Neuronal (RIAN)
bio-inspired.institution: Universidad de Chile, Departments of Physics and Biology
bio-inspired.summary: RIAN studies how biological neuronal networks form, synchronize, adapt and evolve using in-vitro neuronal cultures, biophysical experiments and computational models. Current network activities include modeling spontaneous activity and a data-driven tool for displaying synchrony. The mechanistic study of self-organizing biological networks is explicit; transfer to computational methods is an inference, and the record does not claim an engineered in-vitro computer or separate Bordeu laboratory.
bio-inspired.activity: University of Chile reports RIAN’s current 2026 FALAN and NeuroFest outputs, including computational modeling of piriform-cortex activity and Neurobeat visualization of experimentally recorded synchronized activity in in-vitro neuronal cultures; RNIT 2025 selected the distinct interdepartmental network for funding.

bio-inspired.name: Reddy Lab — learning and distributed computation in multicellular systems
bio-inspired.institution: Princeton University, Department of Physics
bio-inspired.summary: The current PI-led lab explicitly models how individual cells exchange information to coordinate multicellular behavior as distributed computation, including developmental patterning, cell identity changes, and self-organization.
bio-inspired.activity: Current lab page lists active 2025–2026 work on cell fate specification, multicellular organization, and genotype–phenotype mapping; Princeton profile confirms current assistant professor/lab-head role and advises six researchers.

bio-inspired.name: Reena Singh Lab — Cardiovascular Development and 3D Organoid Morphogenesis
bio-inspired.institution: Institute for Stem Cell Science and Regenerative Medicine (inStem)
bio-inspired.summary: The lab directly studies organ-development morphogenesis, progenitor specification and differentiation in human pluripotent-stem-cell-derived 3D organoids. Organ development is explicit; an in-vitro computational or engineered-system bridge is not stated, so the relevance class remains strongly related rather than core.
bio-inspired.activity: Current faculty profile describes active organ-development and hPSC-organoid research; the institute archived-position page lists current 2026 recruitment to Reena Singh Laboratory.

bio-inspired.name: Regeneration Lab (Sumeet Pal Singh)
bio-inspired.institution: Shiv Nadar University, Department of Life Sciences
bio-inspired.summary: The group studies how cell plasticity and adaptation let zebrafish liver/pancreas tissues recover from injury and metabolic stress, with single-cell, live-imaging and gene-editing methods. This directly addresses biological tissue repair and regeneration.
bio-inspired.activity: SNU’s September 2025 profile confirms the current lab, new institution and active zebrafish work; current lab page describes liver regeneration and cellular adaptation.

bio-inspired.name: Research Group for Robotics and Intelligent Systems (Kyrre Glette)
bio-inspired.institution: University of Oslo, Department of Informatics
bio-inspired.summary: The group’s current work spans embodied AI and co-design of robot morphology/control; its 2026 outputs include evolutionary robotics, QD, and a dedicated ALIFE special session on morphology/control co-design.
bio-inspired.activity: Repository lists multiple 2026 publications and ALIFE 2026 special-session activity.

bio-inspired.name: Research Group on Epistemology of the Sciences of the Artificial (RG-ESA) — Synthetic Biology and Embodied AI
bio-inspired.institution: IULM University; University of Bologna; University of Salento
bio-inspired.summary: The current RG-ESA lead coauthored a 2025 framework for chemical-network cognition and protocellular agents; an official 2023–26 collaborative project specifies wetware models of minimal biological cognition and synthetic-biology methods.

bio-inspired.name: Richard Löffler — active-matter and complex chemical systems research programme
bio-inspired.institution: Globe Institute and Centre for Star and Planet Formation, University of Copenhagen
bio-inspired.summary: A current independent-PI programme studies active matter and complex chemical systems as models for life and its origin. Recent work and 2026 experiments examine chemical self-propulsion, dissipative droplet behavior and collective dynamics resembling chemotaxis or swarming. The fit is mechanistic and relevant to basal agency and self-organization, but sources do not establish an engineered artificial-life or computational device, so it remains STRONGLY_RELATED.
bio-inspired.activity: The University of Copenhagen profile identifies Löffler as an independent PI studying active matter/complex chemical systems and life origins. A 2026 NBI seminar details ongoing lab experiments with self-propelled droplets and primitive agency. His peer-reviewed 2024 paper analyzes aggregation of self-propelled rods.

bio-inspired.name: Rita Mateus Group
bio-inspired.institution: TU Dresden, Cluster of Excellence Physics of Life (PoL), Dresden
bio-inspired.summary: The group directly investigates how electrical, chemical, and mechanical signals encode information for proportional organ growth and regeneration.
bio-inspired.activity: Official 2026 news reports current Science Advances work on injury-induced electrochemical coupling, organ growth, and repair; current group page lists active members.

bio-inspired.name: Robert M. Hazen's Origins of Life research group
bio-inspired.institution: Carnegie Institution for Science, Earth & Planets Laboratory
bio-inspired.summary: Hazen’s current group studies prebiotic chemistry in mineral, ocean and atmospheric contexts and constrains plausible origin-of-life pathways through geochemistry. Carnegie’s 2025 work examines molecular signatures of ancient life in rocks, showing current activity.
bio-inspired.activity: Carnegie’s 2025 report names Hazen on a current study applying chemical analysis and machine learning to more than 400 samples, including ancient rocks, fossils, meteorites and living organisms, to detect preserved signatures of life.

bio-inspired.name: Robinson Group
bio-inspired.institution: Institute for Molecules and Materials, Radboud University
bio-inspired.summary: The group studies self-organizing chemical reaction networks as information-processing systems, including chemical reservoir computation and prebiotic reaction networks. Official research pages state the biological inspiration and list current information-processing mechanisms.
bio-inspired.activity: The publications page lists Robinson’s 2026 article on information in chemical reaction systems, 2025 prebiotic-network work and the 2024 reservoir-computation paper; group members page lists current PhD and postdoctoral members.

bio-inspired.name: ROBIOLAB — Bioinspired Robotics Laboratory
bio-inspired.institution: Universidad de los Andes, Department of Mechanical Engineering
bio-inspired.summary: Current ROBIOLAB projects include a parameterized automated search over gripper morphologies, with simulation screening of hundreds of geometries and physical validation. The lab itself calls the process generative design and draws an analogy to evolutionary production of morphology. Its connection to automated discovery is an inference from the documented simulation-guided design search; there is no claim of open-ended evolution or an evolutionary algorithm.
bio-inspired.activity: The lab’s September 30, 2026 article reports active projects including a fish-locomotion-inspired soft robot and underactuated hand. Its project page lists multiple 2026 projects. The coral-gripper page reports hundreds of simulated designs and physical validation.

bio-inspired.name: Robotics Lab (naXys), Autonomous Systems and Robotics group
bio-inspired.institution: University of Namur, Faculty of Computer Science; Namur Institute for Complex Systems (naXys)
bio-inspired.summary: The current lab coordinates research in autonomous robotics and models of natural individual and social behavior. Its active BABOTS project develops controllable biological animal robots by reprogramming worms’ or insects’ nervous systems, while the lab’s evolutionary-robotics work studies collective decision and adaptive swarm behavior. The bridge to bio-inspired robotics is explicit in the current group and project pages.
bio-inspired.activity: Current naXys page lists BABOTS, coordinated by Tuci and funded through 10/2027, and an ongoing collective-decision project using evolutionary robotics (research-assistant period through 2028). It lists Tuci among current staff.

bio-inspired.name: Robotics Lab.@CSE-IIT Guwahati

bio-inspired.summary: Builds networked mobile-robot systems whose distributed agents share information and intelligence using stigmergy and mobile-agent mechanisms, with bio-inspired and artificial-immune learning for embodied cyber-physical systems.
bio-inspired.activity: Official lab listing includes 2025 immune-inspired embodied-intelligence and robot-learning publications, current 2026 thesis work on decentralized multi-robot task allocation, and accepted 2026 papers on multi-robot positioning and adaptive skill discovery.

This is a direct biological-control/computation bridge.

bio-inspired.name: Roy Bar-Ziv Lab — Artificial Cell Systems
bio-inspired.institution: Weizmann Institute of Science, Department of Chemical and Biological Physics
bio-inspired.summary: The current lab reconstitutes artificial cells from programmed DNA compartments, cell-free gene expression and synthetic genetic oscillators, including communicating cell populations and autonomous assembly of ribosomal subunits. This is direct experimental work on synthetic living organization and protocellular systems under the added life theme; no prebiotic-origin claim is made.
bio-inspired.activity: The current Weizmann PI page describes the artificial-cell programme and current self-regenerating protein-synthesis work, citing 2024 and 2025 outputs. The group roster was updated 6 September 2026 and lists the PI and current lab members.

bio-inspired.activity: MIT CSAIL confirms current PhD identity; personal page describes current research on adaptive systems that evolve and learn; 2026 paper on diversity-driven policy optimization has him as first author.

bio-inspired.institution: Schulich Faculty of Chemistry, Technion – Israel Institute of Technology

bio-inspired.activity: Current group publication list includes recent work on experimental information engines and nonequilibrium thermodynamics; the current homepage states that the group is recruiting graduate researchers.

bio-inspired.institution: National University of Kyiv-Mohyla Academy
bio-inspired.summary: Current research program develops neural architectures through explicit developmental encodings and morphogenetic rules; 2025 MorphoNAS-Bench and 2026 MorphoNAS-PL publications/repos show sustained work on this exact indirect/developmental-encoding topic.
bio-inspired.activity: The university’s 2025 journal issue lists his MorphoNAS-Bench paper and current author biography; the 2026 GECCO schedule lists his morphogenetic-network paper.

bio-inspired.name: Sgro Lab
bio-inspired.institution: Janelia Research Campus, Howard Hughes Medical Institute
bio-inspired.summary: Joint theory/experiment asks how groups of cells integrate information about their environment and each other; multicellular coordination, collective behavior and wound healing. This is an explicit Bio theme fit (morphogenesis/self-organization or collective cellular computation).
bio-inspired.activity: Janelia first-party lab page was live and the current official lab-members page listed Allyson Sgro on the lab team at the audit date.

resourcesReview.note: Current identity, activity and scope reviewed; this discovery addition does not claim an exhaustive search of personal team sites or prospective research plans.

bio-inspired.name: Shankar Lab — Soft, Living & Functional Matter
bio-inspired.institution: University of Michigan
bio-inspired.summary: Studies collective patterns and function in living and nonliving materials across molecular, cellular and organismal scales. The lab explicitly investigates biological morphogenesis using theoretical modeling, computational analysis and experiments.
bio-inspired.activity: Current 2026 lab updates document research on immune-cell mechanics and plant morphogenesis, and identify current research activity and active PI role.

bio-inspired.name: Sharpe Group — Multicellular Systems Biology
bio-inspired.institution: European Molecular Biology Laboratory, Barcelona
bio-inspired.summary: Combines biology, imaging, computation and 3D/4D simulation to study how gene networks and cell populations generate limb morphogenesis and spatial patterns; the group develops specific computational tools for this mechanistic programme.
bio-inspired.activity: The current publications list includes LimbNET (2026), a platform for simulating spatial patterns of gene networks in limb development, and LimbLab (2026), a 3D analysis and visualisation pipeline.

researchPlans.title: Future projects and goals
researchPlans.author: James Sharpe

bio-inspired.name: Shashidhara Lab — organ specification, growth and morphogenesis
bio-inspired.institution: National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS-TIFR)
bio-inspired.summary: The group studies mechanisms determining organ size and shape, including cell/tissue placement, cellular mechanics and extracellular-matrix dynamics during Drosophila wing/haltere development. These are direct mechanisms of morphogenesis.
bio-inspired.activity: The current NCBS publications page lists the 2024 study on cellular mechanics and ECM dynamics in differential wing/haltere development; current NCBS lab pages describe the ongoing organ-development programme.

bio-inspired.name: Shenshen Wang Research Group — adaptive immunity and physical immune learning
bio-inspired.institution: University of California, Los Angeles, Department of Physics and Astronomy
bio-inspired.summary: The current Wang group studies adaptive immunity using statistical mechanics and computational modeling. Its 2026 work and seminar describe how immune cells use molecular and mechanical mechanisms to sense antigens, improve recognition and produce memory, directly fitting biological learning and cellular computation.
bio-inspired.activity: The group’s current selected-publications page lists 2024 Physical extraction of antigen and information, 2025 epistatic antibody-fitness work, and 2026 Adaptive mechanical proofreading toward robust yet tunable humoral immunity. An official Academia Sinica seminar in August 2026 describes current immune-learning mechanisms.

bio-inspired.name: ShockLab
bio-inspired.institution: University of Cape Town
bio-inspired.summary: The lab studies how environmental variability and metabolic costs shape evolved neural architectures, explicitly relating biological theory to efficient artificial agents.
bio-inspired.activity: 2025 neural-energy paper and September 2026 continuation on environmental change and evolved neural complexity; current supervised researcher roster.

bio-inspired.name: Shunichi Urayama — self-replicating RNA and hot-spring replicon programme
bio-inspired.institution: University of Tsukuba, Institute of Life and Environmental Sciences
bio-inspired.summary: Urayama’s current researcher-led programme discovers and characterizes RNA replicons in hot-spring ecosystems. The work examines self-replication, ecological inheritance, and the boundary between RNA replicons and cellular life, connecting current molecular virology to origins and organization questions.
bio-inspired.activity: The current Tsukuba record identifies two PI-led grants spanning 2024–26 and 2025–26 plus a 2026 Nature Communications article on hot-spring Obelisk-like RNA replicons and current 2025 talks on the life/non-life boundary.

bio-inspired.name: Sivak Group (David Sivak)
bio-inspired.institution: Simon Fraser University, Department of Physics
bio-inspired.summary: Research links nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, information theory, energy transduction and biological molecular systems.
bio-inspired.activity: Official Fall 2026 page lists current group members and teaching.

bio-inspired.name: SNU Biorobotics Laboratory
bio-inspired.institution: Seoul National University
bio-inspired.summary: The lab explicitly transforms biological structures and movement into soft robotic mechanisms, including beetle-wing-inspired origami, multimodal locomotion and deployable robots. This is a clear mechanism-to-robot bridge; sources do not establish evolutionary-algorithm work.
bio-inspired.activity: The official lab publication list includes multiple 2024–2026 outputs and 2026 papers; the current group roster identifies Kyu-Jin Cho as Professor and lab PI.

bio-inspired.name: SNU Robotics Institute (National Research Laboratory)
bio-inspired.institution: Seoul National University
bio-inspired.summary: SNU’s 2026 ten-year institute programme combines robotic bodies and intelligence, physical/distributed intelligence, and bio-inspired technologies based on living organisms. The large interdisciplinary institute is retained at the umbrella programme level; the roster’s other groups were screened individually and are not automatically treated as Bio units.
bio-inspired.activity: Official SNU announcement dated 2026-08-25 states the institute opened on 2026-08-18 and received a ten-year 2026 NRL 2.0 programme. Current institute site lists 13 research groups and has 2026-10-13 seminar news.

bio-inspired.name: SNU Soft Robotics & Bionics Laboratory
bio-inspired.institution: Seoul National University
bio-inspired.summary: The lab’s current programme mimics the morphology and function of biological muscle-tendon-ligament systems in soft robots. Its 2026 publication list includes a bio-inspired artificial muscle-tendon complex for bidirectional afferent-efferent signaling and a self-adaptive photonic synapse for autonomous neuromorphic robots, an explicit biological-mechanism-to-computation/robotics bridge.
bio-inspired.activity: Official 2026 publication roster lists the synapse, artificial muscle-tendon complex, proprioceptive actuator-control and biomimetic finger work; SNU Robotics directory identifies Yong-Lae Park as Associate Professor leading the laboratory.

bio-inspired.name: Soloveichik Group (UT Austin)
bio-inspired.institution: University of Texas at Austin
bio-inspired.summary: Group uses DNA hybridization and strand-displacement cascades to build molecular interactions for computation and synthetic biology.
bio-inspired.activity: Official group page lists current lab openings and projects; DNA32 2026 proceedings have multiple papers coauthored by Soloveichik.

bio-inspired.name: Soumya Banerjee research programme in neural cellular automata and complex systems
bio-inspired.institution: University of Cambridge, Accelerate Programme
bio-inspired.summary: Cambridge identifies an ongoing project led by Banerjee to study computing and intelligence in biological and artificial complex systems. His current neural cellular automata work explicitly models morphogenesis and self-organization, including learning, growth, persistence and regeneration of patterns.
bio-inspired.activity: Cambridge publications list multiple 2025 NCA studies; the 2025-09-30 ALife study models morphogenesis, reaction-diffusion, self-organization and pattern regeneration. Current Cambridge profile identifies him as Senior Research Associate; the programme page identifies his project as led by him.

bio-inspired.name: SPECS-lab — Synthetic, Perceptive, Emotive and Cognitive Systems
bio-inspired.institution: CSIC Institute of Neuroscience, Universidad Miguel Hernández de Elche
bio-inspired.summary: Develops embodied autonomous systems using synthetic methods to model biological behavioral principles. Current work models homeostatic/allostatic regulation and motivational mechanisms in robots. Its fit to the published Bio themes is strongly related through a specific inferred bridge from biological regulation to embodied robotics; the ALIFE study does not demonstrate evolutionary search or body morphology co-design.
bio-inspired.activity: The lab’s 2025 programme post identifies SPECS-lab at UMH; two 2025 papers in ALIFE and IROS develop robot allostasis and motivational cognitive maps. A 2026 research article confirms Verschure’s current SPECS-lab affiliation at UMH.

bio-inspired.name: Speech, Music and Hearing research group
bio-inspired.institution: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
bio-inspired.summary: The current KTH unit houses the 2025 GECCO quality-diversity search over an articulatory vocal model; current team and 2026 doctoral activity show an ongoing group program where QD is a published method line.
bio-inspired.activity: Official KTH profile identifies Grouwels in Speech, Music & Hearing; 2026 doctoral defense identifies Jonason in Speech and Music Communication; 2025 roster reports the QD output.

bio-inspired.name: Statistical Biophysics @ ENS — Thierry Mora and Aleksandra Walczak Group
bio-inspired.institution: Laboratoire de physique de l’École normale supérieure (LPENS), ENS-PSL
topics: statistical physics and inference for biology
bio-inspired.summary: The PI-led group studies adaptive immune and viral coevolution using statistical physics and inference. Its current immune-learning research is a credible molecular-learning mechanism bridge to cellular/molecular computation and basal cognition; the fit is related rather than direct because the funded programme is described in terms of immune evolution, not computation.
bio-inspired.activity: LPENS announced on 6 November 2025 that Walczak won an ERC Synergy Grant for CoEvolve, describing joint evolutionary study of adaptive immune repertoires and viral populations. The group page identifies Walczak and Thierry Mora as current group leaders and lists active postdoctoral recruitment for the project.

bio-inspired.name: Statistical Physics of Computation Laboratory (SPOC)
bio-inspired.institution: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)
bio-inspired.summary: SPOC studies computational systems and algorithms as interacting-element systems using statistical physics and mathematics. Its current doctoral member Cédric Koller works on cellular-automata dynamics and attractor statistics, with 2024 and 2026 papers on CA fixed points and collective majority dynamics. The connection to cellular computation and artificial-life substrates is direct for this research line but inferred for the lab’s wider programme, so the lab is strongly related rather than core.
bio-inspired.activity: Current SPOC page and roster list active laboratory members and research; 2026 paper by Koller and current SPOC collaborators studies collective majority dynamics, and the 2024 paper studies cellular automata on random graphs.

bio-inspired.name: Steen Rasmussen — protocell and living-technology research programme
bio-inspired.institution: Department of Physics, Chemistry and Pharmacy, University of Southern Denmark
bio-inspired.summary: Rasmussen’s current PI-level work combines an integrated protocell model with molecular replication/inheritable information and energy transduction. The 2025 paper explicitly analyzes how cofactor sequences jointly affect charge transfer, replication and protocell fitness, a direct mechanistic fit to molecular/cellular computation and energy-information coupling.
bio-inspired.activity: The 2025 peer-reviewed paper presents and simulates an integrated protocell where cofactor molecules function both in an electron relay and as replicating information stores, analyzing charge transfer, replication rates and combined fitness. SDU’s current profile identifies Rasmussen’s current departmental role and lists the paper.

bio-inspired.name: Stephen Whitelam Group
bio-inspired.institution: Theory Facility, Molecular Foundry, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
bio-inspired.summary: The group has current explicit methods work in learning algorithms and thermodynamic computing, including training nonlinear stochastic physical computers away from equilibrium. This directly matches the energy-of-computation and learning theme.
bio-inspired.activity: Molecular Foundry’s March 2026 story reports Whitelam’s current nonlinear, nonequilibrium thermodynamic-computer design/training work; his 2025 and 2026 publications are listed on the staff page.

bio-inspired.name: Stuart Group — Self-organisation in the Central Nervous System
bio-inspired.institution: European Molecular Biology Laboratory, Barcelona
bio-inspired.summary: Studies developmental and regenerative self-organisation in neural-tube and spinal-cord organoids using cell/stem-cell biology, mathematical modelling, embryology and bioengineering. This is a direct cellular self-organisation and repair mechanism, not generic neuroscience.
bio-inspired.activity: The publications list includes “Minimal essential requirements for neural tube self-organisation” (2026) and current work on neural organoids and CNS regeneration.

researchPlans.author: Hannah Stuart

bio-inspired.name: Sunil Laxman Lab — Nutrient Sensing and Metabolic Regulation of Cell Fates
bio-inspired.institution: Institute for Stem Cell Science and Regenerative Medicine (inStem)
bio-inspired.summary: Current lab programme explicitly investigates chemical information flow within and between cells, sensing, systems-level information transfer, network logic and cooperation/division of labour among cell groups.
bio-inspired.activity: Current inStem jobportal lists a postdoctoral-fellow recruitment for the Sunil Laxman Lab with a 9 September 2026 deadline; the active faculty page gives the current PI role and ongoing programme.

researchPlans.title: Research statement
researchPlans.author: Sunil Laxman

bio-inspired.name: SymbuLab (Carleton College)
bio-inspired.institution: Carleton College, Department of Computer Science
bio-inspired.summary: SymbuLab develops and uses Symbulation, an open-source agent-based artificial-life and evolution platform to test hypotheses about host–symbiont relationships, including parasitism, commensalism, mutualism, and endosymbiosis. It is an explicit computational model of biological evolutionary mechanisms.
bio-inspired.activity: The ALIFE 2025 proceedings list Vostinar on a paper studying how partner choice enables parasite exclusion in endosymbiotic coevolution. The official ALIFE 2025 page lists the same paper and authors among the best-paper awardees. Current Carleton research page describes the Symbulation methods and target biological systems.

bio-inspired.name: SynBio Araraquara — Danielle Pedrolli research group
bio-inspired.institution: School of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Department of Bioprocess Engineering and Biotechnology, São Paulo State University (UNESP)
bio-inspired.summary: The current SynBio Araraquara programme includes microbial gene-expression regulation and synthetic circuitry. Its 2026 work applies ML to predict and design intrinsic transcription terminators as functional parts of synthetic gene circuits, then validates the designed parts in live E. coli and an in vitro transcription assay. This provides an explicit current molecular gene-regulation mechanism and biologically validated circuit-part design; it is not a claim that all the group’s strain-engineering activity is in scope.
bio-inspired.activity: Current 2026 bioRxiv preprint lists Pedrolli as corresponding author and reports ML-based prediction and design of transcription terminators for synthetic gene circuits, with in vivo E. coli and in vitro validation. The work is a preprint, not peer-reviewed. Current UNESP/FAPESP profiles establish her active group and faculty appointment.

bio-inspired.name: SynBio UFABC — Synthetic Biology research group
bio-inspired.lead: Milca Rachel da Costa Ribeiro Lins
bio-inspired.institution: Center for Natural and Human Sciences, Federal University of ABC (CCNH-UFABC)
bio-inspired.summary: The PI-led SynBio UFABC group explicitly designs and validates synthetic gene circuits in cell-free systems and prokaryotic biological models. Its described biosensor circuitry and cell-free analog-to-digital signal-processing work provide an explicit molecular information-processing mechanism within the cellular/molecular-computation theme. Current 2026 funding supports active programme status; the record does not extend that fit to all synthetic biology or metabolic engineering work in the group.
bio-inspired.activity: FAPESP record shows an active award led by Lins at UFABC from 2026-03-01 to 2029-02-28, with synthetic antisense RNAs, CRISPR-Cas9 and bioinformatics/wet-lab methods. The UFABC research-profile page records ongoing research and the group’s current circuit programme, including its 2023 cell-free biosensor analog-to-digital converter paper and 2024 supervised circuit projects.

bio-inspired.name: SynBioLab UnB — Genetic Circuits and Synthetic Biology
bio-inspired.institution: University of Brasília (UnB), Institute of Biological Sciences, Department of Genetics and Morphology
bio-inspired.summary: PI-led synthetic biology lab develops genetic switches and other molecular tools for controlling gene expression and sensing nucleic acids, plus methods to reduce prokaryotic genomes. Genetic circuits and molecular sensing/control implement information-processing functions in biological substrates.
bio-inspired.activity: The current UnB faculty profile lists the 2025 SynBio congress outputs and technical work; the current UnB laboratory directory maintains the group under Coelho and lists active research projects in synthetic gene control and detection.

bio-inspired.name: SynCell Asia Initiative — synthetic-cell roadmap programme
bio-inspired.institution: Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, with participating institutions across six Asian countries
bio-inspired.summary: A current multi-country collaborative programme to build a synthetic cell from nonliving biomolecules and explain emergence of cellular life. Its published roadmap specifies machine-learning-supported design-build-test-learn, cellular digital twins, autonomous ribosome regeneration, self-replication and environmental evolution.
bio-inspired.activity: 2026-05-26 Nature Biotechnology roadmap; official SIAT/CAS pages report a 2023-founded initiative and an active ten-year ProtoCell-to-AutoCell programme. The programme includes ongoing consortium workshops and explicit 2026 design/research targets.

bio-inspired.name: Synthetic Biology and Molecular Computing Lab
bio-inspired.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH)
bio-inspired.summary: POSTECH's current lab publications include 2024 work on signal processing/cellular control and cell-free multilayer gene circuits, and 2026 RATEX RNA-based multi-layered cellular programming, programmable translational control and genetic-circuit stability. The current lab page is recruiting; the member roster identifies Professor Jongmin Kim as PI.
bio-inspired.activity: POSTECH's current lab publications include 2024 work on signal processing/cellular control and cell-free multilayer gene circuits, and 2026 RATEX RNA-based multi-layered cellular programming, programmable translational control and genetic-circuit stability. The current lab page is recruiting; the member roster identifies Professor Jongmin Kim as PI.

bio-inspired.name: Synthetic Biology Laboratory — Masayuki Su’etsugu
bio-inspired.institution: Rikkyo University, College of Science, Department of Life Science
bio-inspired.summary: The laboratory explicitly seeks to reconstruct self-replicating, evolving cells. It combines in-vitro genome replication and gene-expression systems with synthetic genomes; recent work has demonstrated self-replication of long artificial genomic DNA and self-growing protocell models.
bio-inspired.activity: JST reported on 2026-08-19 that Su’etsugu’s Rikkyo group constructed 53-kb artificial genomic DNA encoding 26 replication proteins and repeatedly self-replicated it in a cell-free system through serial passage. The 2025 JST release separately documents a collaborative self-growing protocell model with DNA replication linked to gene expression.

bio-inspired.name: Synthetic Biology Research Center (SBRC)
bio-inspired.institution: Korea Research Institute of Bioscience and Biotechnology (KRIBB)
bio-inspired.summary: The directly fetched official center page describes artificial genetic circuits in a digitally integrated DBTL program, with programmable probiotics and microbial consortia, explicitly connecting synthetic biology to AI-driven biofoundry innovation and genetic-circuit design. This is a direct fit to cellular/molecular computation, not a claim that all industrial synthetic biology is computational.
bio-inspired.activity: Directly fetched official NST page lists current SBRC functions, achievements including K-Biofoundry and programmable microbial systems, and Dae-Hee Lee as Associate Director, with 2024 awards in his profile.

bio-inspired.name: Synthetic Biology Research Group — Sangram Bagh
bio-inspired.institution: Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics, Biophysics and Structural Genomics Division; Homi Bhabha National Institute
bio-inspired.summary: The group engineers molecular genetic circuits as computational devices inside bacterial cells and combines engineered cells into multicellular artificial-neural-network architectures. A current 2026 institutional intake names the Biological Artificial Intelligence programme and a July 2026 corresponding-author paper demonstrates multicellular cellular computation.
bio-inspired.activity: SINP’s current August 2026 graduate intake names Bagh’s Synthetic Molecular Biology, Cellular Engineering and Biological Artificial Intelligence research area. On July 28, 2026, the group published a primary paper, with Bagh corresponding author, in which engineered bacteria collectively compute classifications of four prime-number families. Its 2024 primary paper demonstrated multicellular neural-network-type cellular computation.

bio-inspired.name: Synthetic BioSystems Design Lab (Wang Lab)
bio-inspired.institution: Zhejiang University Hangzhou Global Science and Technology Innovation Center / ZJU-HIC
bio-inspired.summary: The PI-led group explicitly engineers circuits to compute cellular/environmental signals. Its 2025 report documents RNA trans-splicing/protein-splicing circuits implementing multi-input cellular logic gates, including six-input AND computation.
bio-inspired.activity: First-party research report dated 2025-01-02 describes the Nature Chemical Biology 2025 paper on programmable RNA circuits; current lab homepage links it as latest news.

bio-inspired.name: Systems Biology & Computational Biochemistry Laboratory (Nagasuma Chandra)
bio-inspired.institution: IISc, Department of Biochemistry
bio-inspired.summary: The group combines computational systems biology with experimental host-pathogen research. Its 2023 regulatory-barcode study shows perturbing a gene-control barcode shifts macrophage polarization destination, a direct cell-fate control mechanism. The Bio-inspired relevance is through biological molecular decision logic.
bio-inspired.activity: Current lab roster and 2025–2026 publications show ongoing activity; lab publication list includes the 2023 macrophage regulatory-barcode cell-fate paper.

bio-inspired.name: Systems Biology Laboratory — cellular signalling, gene regulation and information processing
bio-inspired.institution: Centro Regional de Estudios Genómicos (CREG), Facultad de Ciencias Exactas, Universidad Nacional de La Plata (UNLP); CENEXA-CONICET-UNLP
bio-inspired.summary: The laboratory models how molecular and environmental signals are integrated into cellular responses. Its current methods include stochastic models of gene regulatory networks, promoter/enhancer dynamics, information-theoretic analysis, systems dynamics and experimental validation. This is a direct mechanistic programme in cellular information processing, not generic systems biology.
bio-inspired.activity: Official current laboratory page calls Diambra the group leader and describes ongoing/current projects; current CENEXA investigator listing identifies him as Principal Investigator. The lab page includes active research lines and a 2025 copyright footer.

bio-inspired.name: Szostak Lab
bio-inspired.institution: Department of Chemistry, University of Chicago
topics: transition from chemical to Darwinian evolution
bio-inspired.summary: The current faculty programme explicitly investigates how life could emerge through self-replicating nucleic-acid genomes and cell boundaries, and develops artificial-cell models to test the transition from chemical to Darwinian evolution. A 2025 study on a self-sustaining chimeric ribozyme demonstrates current mechanistic research. Count one PI lab; the Center for Origins of Life is not separately counted here.
bio-inspired.activity: University of Chicago report dated April 16, 2025 describes a Szostak Lab study on a self-sustaining chimeric ribozyme assembled from RNA and amino-acid components.

bio-inspired.name: Takahiro Sagawa — information thermodynamics research programme
bio-inspired.institution: The University of Tokyo
bio-inspired.summary: Current theory programme studies information thermodynamics and thermodynamic design limits for information processing.
bio-inspired.activity: Current professor profile plus 2026 project plan on topology, nonequilibrium systems, thermodynamics, energy-efficient devices.
