bio-inspired.name: Takato Horii Research Programme (Osaka University)
bio-inspired.institution: Osaka University, Graduate School of Engineering Science
bio-inspired.summary: The current programme explicitly identifies cognitive developmental robotics and computational models of development, with embodied robot learning and active inference. Developmental robotics is a named Bio-inspired theme; the record does not imply that all programme projects are biologically motivated.
bio-inspired.activity: Current list includes 2026 ALIFE and robotics outputs, 2025 embodied-robotics/developmental and multi-agent outputs, and the October 2025 ALIFE swarm-oscillator paper; current page reports ongoing Associate Professor programme and recent 2026 group news.

bio-inspired.name: Takeshi Kakegawa — Early Earth and Origin-of-Life Geochemistry Programme
bio-inspired.institution: Tohoku University Graduate School of Science, Department of Earth Science
bio-inspired.summary: Kakegawa’s programme combines ancient-rock and hydrothermal geological/geochemical investigation with simulations of early-Earth prebiotic synthesis, addressing environmental mechanisms relevant to life’s origin.
bio-inspired.activity: Kakegawa’s programme combines ancient-rock and hydrothermal geological/geochemical investigation with simulations of early-Earth prebiotic synthesis, addressing environmental mechanisms relevant to life’s origin.

bio-inspired.name: Taniguchi Laboratory / Symbol Emergence Systems Group (Kyoto continuation of existing R0271)
bio-inspired.institution: Kyoto University, Graduate School of Informatics
bio-inspired.summary: The current lab explicitly studies how meaning, language and symbols emerge through interactions among humans, robots and AI agents, using constructive cognitive developmental robotics. The connection to self-organisation is inferred from the programme’s agent-interaction and emergence mechanisms; this does not claim biological morphogenesis.
bio-inspired.activity: Official publications page updated 2026-04-02 lists 2026 and 2025 work in continuous symbol emergence, decentralized collective world models, emergent communication, and multi-agent robotics; the current member roster lists professor Taniguchi and the Kyoto group.

bio-inspired.name: TAPDANCE: Theory And Practice of DNA Computing Engines
bio-inspired.institution: Hamilton Institute, Maynooth University
bio-inspired.summary: Current group develops DNA molecular computers through theory and laboratory implementation.
bio-inspired.activity: Current page lists 2026 publications, grant funding and active researchers; Woods is a 2026 DNA paper coauthor.

bio-inspired.name: Terasaka Laboratory
bio-inspired.institution: Earth-Life Science Institute (ELSI), Institute of Science Tokyo
bio-inspired.summary: A separately named, active PI-led laboratory links experimental molecular engineering with origin-of-life mechanisms and synthetic biology.
bio-inspired.activity: The lab site says it began June 2022 and lists a recent (October 2026) news item about a cell-free protein expression paper and a new doctoral student; current official ELSI roster lists Terasaka as Associate PI.

bio-inspired.name: Terence Kee Abiogenesis and Cellular Emergence Programme
bio-inspired.institution: School of Chemistry, University of Leeds
bio-inspired.summary: Kee’s current profile states an active programme studying fundamental processes relevant to cellular emergence, including self-assembly and molecular diffusion in geologically relevant hydrogels and metabolic-simulant coupling to gel-scale behaviour.
bio-inspired.activity: Current Leeds staff page identifies Kee as Reader and describes his continuing research interests and programme.

bio-inspired.name: The Biological Computing Company
bio-inspired.institution: The Biological Computing Company
bio-inspired.summary: The company grows real neural cultures, stimulates them and derives computational principles converted into software layers that improve AI models, plus a roadmap for neurons and silicon computing together.
bio-inspired.activity: Site pages describe the world's first neuron-derived video model and current discovery work using neural cultures.

bio-inspired.name: The DasGupta Laboratory
bio-inspired.institution: University of Notre Dame, Department of Chemistry & Biochemistry
bio-inspired.summary: The current PI-led laboratory evolves RNA catalysts and constructs model protocells to study how RNA systems can exhibit growth, division, competition and Darwinian evolution.
bio-inspired.activity: Current Notre Dame faculty profile identifies the assistant professor and lab; the lab’s 2026 recruitment notice describes current origin-of-life, in-vitro RNA evolution and synthetic cell work. Official profiles list 2026 and 2025 ribozyme/prebiotic publications.

bio-inspired.name: The Huck Group
bio-inspired.institution: Institute for Molecules and Materials, Radboud University
bio-inspired.summary: A protease reaction network functions as a reservoir computer that processes glucose-linked signals; current in-vitro enzymatic-network research is explicit molecular computation.
bio-inspired.activity: The group posted two papers in May 2026: an enzymatic reservoir-computing sensor that performs information-processing tasks and a model-guided in-vitro enzymatic-network design method.

bio-inspired.name: The Krishnamurthy Lab — Prebiotic Chemistry, Protometabolism and Protocells
bio-inspired.institution: Scripps Research, Department of Chemistry
bio-inspired.summary: The laboratory explicitly studies chemical mechanisms in life’s origins, including the emergence of informational polymers, protometabolic reaction networks with potential for self-sustaining cycles, and the transition from prebiotic vesicles to protocells. Recent work experimentally tests prebiotically plausible reaction pathways toward RNA precursors.
bio-inspired.activity: In a 2025 paper (first published 2025-06-27), the lab showed that diamidophosphate phosphorylation of mixed pentoses selectively produces ribofuranose-derived cyclic phosphates, offering an abiotic route toward RNA. The current lab publications page lists additional 2025 work on protometabolic pathways and prebiotic chemistry; the current roster includes active postdoctoral researchers and graduate researchers.

bio-inspired.name: The Moran Research Group — Joseph Moran
bio-inspired.institution: University of Ottawa; affiliated with ISIS, University of Strasbourg
bio-inspired.summary: The group studies how biological metabolism could emerge from prebiotic chemistry, experimentally testing enzyme-free reactions and networks and aiming to generate interacting abiotic systems with lifelike properties.
bio-inspired.activity: The current faculty profile lists 2024–2025 origin/metabolism publications and active graduate recruitment; the lab describes an ongoing self-organized reaction-network programme.

bio-inspired.name: The PUSH Lab
bio-inspired.institution: Amherst College; associated researchers at UMass Amherst and Hampshire College
bio-inspired.summary: Develops evolving-program languages and selection methods, including lexicase selection, diversity-driven search and artificial-life systems.
bio-inspired.activity: The current primary lab roster identifies Spector as director and distinguishes recently active members from past associates. Amherst’s current faculty page lists2024 open-ended quality-diversity methods,2025 dominated novelty search and2026 research.

bio-inspired.name: The Thom Group — prebiotic reaction-network programme
bio-inspired.institution: Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry, University of Cambridge
bio-inspired.summary: An official current project page names Alex Thom as lead supervisor for a project building automated reaction networks for prebiotic environments from quantum-chemical calculations with uncertainty propagation. Current group roster lists presenter Tamara Buja as a postgraduate researcher. This is one PI-led programme, not a separate student unit.
bio-inspired.activity: Current LCLU research-proposals page lists the project “Simulating Reaction networks for prebiotic environments,” lead supervisor Alex Thom and automated network/quantum-chemical methods; current Thom Group roster lists Tamara Buja as a postgraduate student.

bio-inspired.name: Theoretical / Protocell Biophysics (Biofisika Institute)
bio-inspired.lead: Kepa Ruiz-Mirazo and Daniele De Martino
bio-inspired.institution: Biofisika Institute (CSIC, University of the Basque Country / EHU)
bio-inspired.summary: The current group studies how biological organization originates through metabolic processes and membrane compartments. Its current publications include computational models of evolving protocell agency and metabolism, spatially distributed multicellular metabolic coordination, and intercellular metabolic networks.
bio-inspired.activity: Current official group page lists its named co-leaders, staff and 2025 papers on evolving protocell ecologies, intercellular metabolic networks, and metabolic coordination/phase transitions in multicellular systems.

bio-inspired.name: Theoretical Approaches in Cell Biology / Physics of Active, Evolving Systems (Madan Rao)
bio-inspired.institution: National Centre for Biological Sciences, TIFR
bio-inspired.summary: Investigates how active cellular organization and mechanics support information processing, computation and control, including pattern formation and morphogenesis.
bio-inspired.activity: The official publication list includes 2024–25 active-matter work; a 2025 APS paper develops a model of traveling mechanical waves in renewable active matter with cellular implications. The NCBS annual report records retirement in 2025, so this is retained as an active emeritus research program rather than a current faculty position.

bio-inspired.name: Theoretical Biochemistry Group (University of Vienna)
bio-inspired.lead: Ivo L. Hofacker (group head); Christoph Flamm (chemical-reaction-network research lead)
bio-inspired.institution: University of Vienna, Faculty of Chemistry, Institute for Theoretical Chemistry
bio-inspired.summary: The group develops computational methods for RNA structure/design and chemical reaction networks, including graph grammars to model biochemical reactions and evolving catalyzed networks. ai-for-science.summary: FrontierOR builds a literature-grounded benchmark of 180 large-scale operations-research tasks to evaluate whether LLMs can design scalable algorithms that exploit mathematical problem structure, beyond translating a natural-language prompt into a solver formulation. Each task includes a mathematical formulation, standardized instances, Gurobi reference baseline, feasibility checker and hidden expert-verified evaluation; the maintained project adds hardened agent evaluation and self-evolution analysis. This is a specific AI-methods programme for mathematical optimization and algorithm design. Its fit as an independent census unit and relation to the authors’ home labs require root review.
ai-for-science.activity: Official project news records the FrontierOR-v1 dataset update on 2026-09-27, NeurIPS 2026 Evaluation & Dataset Track acceptance on 2026-09-24, trusted-evaluation infrastructure added in August 2026, and a live 180-task benchmark. The official site names 27 people on the Research Team, including project lead Ao Qu.
